دليل المستخدم مولَّد بالذكاء الاصطناعي / AI generated

وصف مولد تلقائياً، مشتق من حيث المحتوى من وثائق AUTOSAR R25-11 المشار إليها (مواصفة SWS والوثائق المعيارية المصاحبة) — وليس نصاً رسمياً لـ AUTOSAR. العبارات المعلّمة بأنها تفسير هي استنتاجات من المصادر.

نموذج الاتصال

ara::com هي واجهة التطبيق الموحدة لمجموعة وظائف إدارة الاتصالات. تقوم المجموعة ببناء ومراقبة مسارات الاتصال بين التطبيقات الموجودة على نفس الأجهزة أو على أجهزة مختلفة؛ ومع ذلك، تظل بنية البرامج الوسيطة الداخلية المحددة مسألة تنفيذ. SWS CM §7.1.1 «Architectural concepts» و SWS CM §7.1.2 «Design decisions» يصنفان API كواجهة مجردة من البروتوكول وموجهة نحو الخدمة.

ينشأ من Service Interface مُنمذج دوران: Proxy هو التمثيل المحلي لـ Consumer، وSkeleton يصل تنفيذ Provider ببنية النقل. Methods وEvents وFields وTriggers هي أشكال الاتصال الأربعة المخصصة. تصف EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 «Proxy/Skeleton Architecture» وEXP ARAComAPI §4.2 «Means of Communication» وSWS CM §7.1.3 «Communication paradigms and Definitions» هذا التقسيم للعمل.

من عرض الخدمة إلى الاستخدام

يُنشأ Skeleton ويُعرض من جانب Provider. ومن جانب Consumer، يوفر FindService لمرة واحدة المثيلات المعروفة حاليًا؛ ويراقب StartFindService تغييرات التوافر. ويعرّف Handle مثيلًا تم العثور عليه ويُستخدم لإنشاء Proxy. وعند عدم التوافر المؤقت، ينبغي إعادة إنشاء مسار الاتصال عند عرض لاحق. توفر SWS CM §7.5.1 «Offer service» وSWS CM §7.5.10 «Find service» وSWS CM §7.5.11 «Service proxy creation» دلالات الوظيفة.

نماذج البيانات والتفاعل

تنقل الأحداث البيانات إلى المستهلكين المسجلين؛ تستخدم المشغلات نفس آلية الاشتراك بدون حمولة. نموذج الطلب/الاستجابة للأساليب ويمكن أن يوفر Future. يجمع الحقل بين حرف طريقة القراءة والكتابة مع إشعار بتغييرات القيمة. يشرح EXP ARAComAPI §4.3 «Event and Trigger based communication» وEXP ARAComAPI §4.4 «Method based communication» وEXP ARAComAPI §4.5 «Field based communication» طريقة عرض التطبيق.

قواعد التشغيل وسياق الأمان

Subscribe() غير متزامن: فقط kSubscribed في الحالة أو الحالة-Handler يحتل Subscription الذي تم إنشاؤه بالفعل. تخضع العينات المستلمة لعملية نقل ملكية خاضعة للرقابة ويجب إعادتها قبل إلغاء التسجيل أو تدمير Proxy. [SWS_CM_12006] و [SWS_CM_00085] هي القواعد ذات الصلة بذلك. تكمل حماية E2E عملية نقل البيانات بمعلومات الحالة التي يمكن تقييمها لكل عينة؛ يمكن لـ SecOC نشر Freshness-Value-Management عبر امتداد النظام الأساسي. SWS CM §7.4 «Safety» وSWS CM §7.3.2 «Secure Communication» يوفران الإطار الشامل.

مرجع المثيل والتجريد الملزم

يستخدم كود التطبيق عادةً InstanceSpecifier منطقيًا؛ ويحلله Manifest إلى InstanceIdentifier واحد أو أكثر خاص بالربط. بذلك يمكن لكود التطبيق نفسه العمل مع ربط مختلف من جانب Deployment دون تفسير تمثيله. تصف EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 «Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers» وSWS CM §7.5.21 «Instance Specifier Translation» الترجمة.

التعاون: يقوم نموذج ZXQK0000QXZ بإنشاء الأدوار المتعلقة بالتطبيق؛ السند يتوسط التواصل. المصادر: SWS CM §7.1.1 «Architectural concepts»، EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 «Proxy/Skeleton Architecture».

التسلسل: يقوم الاكتشاف بتسليم المقابض؛ يؤدي هذا إلى إنشاء وكيل صالح للاستخدام. تعتبر إعادة الاتصال التلقائي للوكيل الموجود سلوكًا محددًا في وقت التشغيل. المصادر: SWS CM §7.5.10 «Find service»، SWS CM §7.5.11 «Service proxy creation».

التسلسل: نتيجة الاشتراك غير متزامنة؛ يأخذ التطبيق العينات فقط بعد الإخطار ويطلقها قبل تسجيل الخروج. المصادر: SWS CM §7.5.13 «Service event subscription»، SWS CM §7.5.14 «Receive event».

مخطط الحالة: على جانب Proxy، يشير kSubscriptionPending إلى Subscription لم تُنشأ بعد أو انقطعت بسبب عدم التوافر. المصدر: SWS CM §7.5.13 «Service event subscription».

التسلسل: يجمع Field قراءة/كتابة شبيهة بـ Method وتحديثات شبيهة بـ Event؛ ويوفر Set-Handler القيمة الفعلية. المراجع: SWS CM §7.5.8 «Registering get handlers for fields»، SWS CM §7.5.9 «Registering set handlers for fields».

مخطط الحالة: يحدد الوضع المختار في Skeleton ما إذا كان التطبيق يجلب الطرق أو ما إذا كان Communication Management ينشطها بالتوازي أو بالتسلسل. المصدر: SWS CM §7.5.6 «Processing of service methods».

مخطط نشاط: يُعيَّن فحص E2E إلى حالة Sample؛ وتقيّم التطبيقات ProfileCheckStatus الفردي. المصدر: SWS CM §7.4.1 «End-to-end communication protection for SOMEIP».

تعاون: توفر أو تتحقق توسعة المنصة FVM من قيم Freshness لـ SecOC؛ وتُعطى حالة التحقق إلى واجهة الحالة المكوَّنة. المصادر: SWS CM §7.3.2 «Secure Communication»، EXP SW Architecture §9.3.1.1.3 «Interfaces for freshness value management».

مخطط النشاط: يتم تعيين InstanceSpecifier المنطقي مقابل Manifest لواحد أو أكثر من المعرفات الخاصة بالربط. المصدر: EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 «Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers».

التصرف في حالة الخطأ

يقوم البحث عن الخدمة لمرة واحدة FindService() بإرجاع مؤشرات الخدمة المناسبة في ذلك الوقت؛ يمكن أن تكون قائمة النتائج فارغة في حالة عدم وجود مثيل خدمة مناسب حاليًا. من ناحية أخرى، يتم الإبلاغ عن خطأ بحث فني على أنه خطأ ara::core::Result، والذي تحدد له واجهة برمجة التطبيقات، من بين أشياء أخرى، ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure. يُبلغ البحث المستمر باستخدام StartFindService() عن تغيرات التوفر عبر معالجه، الذي يتلقى حاوية جميع المثيلات المطابقة. EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.2 «RadarService Proxy Class Example» [SWS_CM_00122] [SWS_CM_00383]

يشتمل اشتراك الحدث على الحالات kNotSubscribed وkSubscriptionPending وkSubscribed. نظرًا لأن Subscribe() يقبل في البداية طلب الاشتراك فقط، فمن الممكن أن تظل الحالة عند الاستعلام عنها هي kSubscriptionPending؛ GetSubscriptionState() وSetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler() يجعلان الحالة الفعالة متاحة. إذا أصبحت الخدمة غير متاحة مؤقتًا، فسيقوم المعالج بالإبلاغ عن kSubscriptionPending؛ بعد إعادة الاشتراك الناجح فإنه تقارير kSubscribed. يجب أن يقوم تطبيق إدارة الاتصالات باستعادة الاشتراك النشط بعد عدم التوفر المؤقت. إذا كان التطبيق يحتوي على كائنات SamplePtr أكثر من تلك الموعودة لـ Subscribe()، فإن GetNewSamples() ترجع الخطأ ComErrc::kMaxSamplesExceeded؛ ربما تم تخطي العينات. [SWS_CM_00310] [SWS_CM_00333] [SWS_CM_00315] [SWS_CM_00701] EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 «Monitoring Event Subscription»

مخطط الحالة: فقدان الخدمة Event-Abonnements وانتقالات الاسترداد التلقائي. المصادر: [SWS_CM_00310] [SWS_CM_00315] EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 «Monitoring Event Subscription».

يقوم استدعاء أسلوب Request/Response بإرجاع ara::core::Future<Output> على الفور. وعبره يتم الاستعلام عن النتيجة والأخطاء المحتملة: بالنسبة لاستجابة خطأ تطبيق تم تكوينها، تحتوي النتيجة على ara::core::ErrorCode من نطاق ApApplicationError؛ وبالنسبة لخدمة لم تعد متوفرة يُحدَّد ComErrc::kServiceNotAvailable. إذا اكتشفت المنصة محليًا خطأً يؤدي إلى فشل الاستدعاء البعيد الذي تم إطلاقه بالفعل، فيجب عليها توفير الـ Future المرتبط مع ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure. لا يوفر ara::com مراقبة مهلة خاصة به لاستدعاءات الأساليب؛ لذلك عند فقدان الاستجابة يمكن أن تنتظر عمليات Future الحاجبة إلى أجل غير مسمى. [SWS_CM_00196] [SWS_CM_10440] SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 «E2E error notification» SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.6 «Timeout supervision»

مخطط التسلسل: يوفر استدعاء أسلوب الطلب/الاستجابة أخطاء في التطبيق والتوفر عبر Future الذي تم إرجاعه. المشاركون المرتبطون هم APPLICATION INTERFACE. المصادر: [SWS_CM_00196] [SWS_CM_10440] SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 «E2E error notification».

بالنسبة إلى E2E-محمية Events، يمكن للتطبيق رؤية نتيجة التحقق E2E لكل SamplePtr مع GetProfileCheckStatus()، على سبيل المثال kOk، kRepeated، kWrongSequence أو kError. يقوم SMState بتكثيف سجل الاختبار إلى المراقبة الحالية E2E؛ يمكن استخدام آخر عينة تم فحصها فقط مع kValid وحالة ملف التعريف غير الصحيحة. إذا فشل التحقق E2E لاستجابة الطريقة، فإن التنفيذ يضع خطأ من ara::com::e2e::ComE2EErrorDomain في Promise المرتبط وبالتالي في النتيجة Future. [SWS_CM_90420] [SWS_CM_90421] [SWS_CM_12021] [SWS_CM_90422] [SWS_CM_90477]

أدلة تفصيلية إضافية

يتم الاحتفاظ بمراجع المواصفات التالية المستخدمة في الوصف السابق للمراجعة المتعمقة: Proxy، [SWS_CM_10438]، [SWS_CM_00122]، [SWS_CM_00622]، [SWS_CM_00209]، [SWS_CM_00123]، [SWS_CM_00623]، Skeleton، [SWS_CM_00101]، [SWS_CM_00201]، [SWS_CM_00203]، [SWS_CM_12002]، ، [SWS_CM_00112]، [SWS_CM_00113]، [SWS_CM_11601]، [SWS_CM_11602]، [SWS_CM_11610]، ، [SWS_CM_00723]، [SWS_CM_00810]، SamplePtr، [SWS_CM_00701]، [SWS_CM_10441]، [SWS_CM_10308]، HandleType، [SWS_CM_00349]، [SWS_CM_00317]، [SWS_CM_00318]، [SWS_CM_11371]، [SWS_CORE_00090]، [SWS_CM_00085]، [SWS_CM_00087]، [SWS_CM_00707]، [SWS_CORE_15002]، [RS_AP_00155]، [SWS_CM_11334]، [SWS_CM_11335]، [SWS_CM_12510]، [SWS_CM_12511]، [SWS_CM_12521]، [SWS_CM_12522]، [RS_AP_00142]، [RS_AP_00119]، [SWS_CM_90413]، [SWS_CM_00042]، [RS_AP_00164]، [SWS_CM_00118]، [TPS_MANI_01017]، [TR_AMETH_00251]، [TR_AMETH_00008]، [TR_AMETH_00012]، [SWS_LBAP_00037]، [SWS_LBAP_00003]، [SWS_LBAP_00050]، [SWS_LBAP_00051]، [SWS_CORE_00055]، [SWS_CORE_90024]، EXP SWArchitecture §9.3 «Communication»، TPS ManifestSpecification §4.2 «Service Interface»، EXP SWArchitecture §13.15 «Service-Oriented Communication»، EXP ARAComAPI §3 «Introduction»، EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 «Proxy/Skeleton Architecture».

من الـ Manifest إلى الفئة المولَّدة مولَّد بالذكاء الاصطناعي / AI generated

تعليمات يتم إنشاؤها تلقائيًا، محتوى مشتق من عناصر مواصفات AUTOSAR-R25-11 المشار إليها - وليس نص AUTOSAR الرسمي. الأدلة: [SWS_…] المراجع.

1. النمذجة في Manifest

نقطة البداية هي ServiceInterface في ARXML-ZXQK0000QXZ (وصف ZXQK0001QXZ). تم تصميم عناصر الخدمة هناك: Events، Methods (بما في ذلك النار والنسيان)، Fields (مع Get/Set/Notifier) وNamespace-Hierarchie للواجهة.

2. ما ينتجه المولد

تقوم أدوات المكدس AP بإنشاء روابط C++ من ZXQK0000QXZ، كل ZXQK0001QXZ (<SI>) فئتان مركزيتان:

  • صنف Skeleton <SI-Namespace>::skeleton::<SI>Skeleton [SWS_CM_00002] في الترويسة <si>_skeleton.h — صنف الأساس من جانب الخادم لمزود الخدمة.
  • فئة Proxy <SI-Namespace>::proxy::<SI>Proxy [SWS_CM_00004] في Header <si>_proxy.h — البديل من جهة العميل.

ينشأ لكل Event وField وMethod أيضًا أصناف داخلية في Namespaces events وfields وmethods (مثلًا <SI-Namespace>::proxy::events::<Event>). توثق صفحات الأصناف النائبة لهذه الوحدة (الأسماء التي تتضمن <…>) هذه الأنواع المولّدة تحديدًا.

3. عرض الخدمة (جانب Skeleton)

  • اشتق فئة التنفيذ الخاصة بك من <SI>Skeleton والفئات الافتراضية البحتة تجاوز طرق الخدمة: توفر الطرق العادية ara::core::Future<…Output> [SWS_CM_00191]، Fire&ننسى الطرق void [SWS_CM_90434].
  • أنشئ مثيلًا بـ ara::core::InstanceSpecifier؛ ويتحكم Processing Mode ‏(MethodCallProcessingMode: kEvent، kEventSingleThread، kPoll) في معالجة الاستدعاءات الواردة [SWS_CM_00301].
  • تقديم الخدمة مع OfferService() [SWS_CM_00101] ومع StopOfferService() استعادة [SWS_CM_00111].
  • تنشر Events عبر events::<Event>::Send() ‏[SWS_CM_00162]، وتحدّث Fields عبر fields::<Field>::Update() ‏[SWS_CM_00119].

4. استخدم الخدمة (صفحة Proxy)

  • البحث عن المثيلات المتاحة: بشكل متزامن عبر <SI>Proxy::FindService() [SWS_CM_00122] (مع InstanceSpecifier [SWS_CM_00622]) أو بشكل مستمر عبر StartFindService() [SWS_CM_11352] [SWS_CM_11365].
  • النتيجة هي <SI>Proxy::HandleType [SWS_CM_00312]؛ ويُنشأ منه Proxy عبر Factory الساكنة <SI>Proxy::Create() [SWS_CM_10438] (يمكن استرجاع Handle لاحقاً عبر GetHandle() [SWS_CM_10383]).
  • الأحداث: events::<Event>::Subscribe() [SWS_CM_00141]، الاستقبال عبر GetNewSamples() [SWS_CM_00701].
  • الحقول: fields::<Field>::Get() [SWS_CM_00112] / Set() [SWS_CM_00113]؛ تُنفذ استدعاءات الطرق بصورة غير متزامنة وتعيد ara::core::Future.

Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

ERWARTETES AUSGABEFORMAT:
Antworte AUSSCHLIESSLICH im validen JSON-Format gemäß folgendem Schema:
Erwartete Ausgabe: JSON-Datei mit demselben Namen wie dieser Auftrag,
Endung .out.json statt .json, im selben Verzeichnis. Aufbau:
{"ergebnisse": [{
  "fragment":  "<wie im Auftrag>",
  "html":      "<vollständiges <div class=\"ai …\">-Fragment, deutsch>",
  "diagramme": {"<pfad relativ zu _src>": "<Quelltext .dot | .seq.json>"},
  "trace": {"prompt": "<der bearbeitete Auftragstext>",
            "modell": "<verwendetes Modell>",
            "wissen":   [{"aussage": "...", "quelle": "<dok-id>", "fundstelle": "..."}],
            "annahmen": [{"annahme": "...", "begruendung": "..."}],
            "transkript": "<Denkprozess/Begründungsgang dieses Laufs>",
            "diagramme": {"<pfad>": {"entscheidung": "...", "annahmen": [...],
                                     "transkript": "..."}}}}]}
Alle Vorgaben aus policy und richtlinien sind bindend (Belegpflicht,
Annahmen-Budget, Diagramm-Kriterien, ai-note, deutsche Sprache).

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P1_02",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 1,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "\u000f\nCommunication Groups are now\nOBSOLETE\n\u000f\nRemoved Raw Data Stream functionality\nfrom ara::com\n\u000f\nAdded new API for checking\nSubscription state on skeleton side\n\u000f\nHarmonization of ara::com API Error\nCodes\n\u000f\nAdded clarifications for SOME/IP-SD\nprotocol usage\n\u000f\nReworked usage of Access\nManagement grants in the ara::com API\n\u000f\nSpecified lifetime requirements for event\nsample data\n\u000f\nStructural changes for better overview\n\u000f\nEditorial changes and bugfixes"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P2_03",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 2,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P2_04",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 2,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "\u000f\nAdded Static Service Connections\n\u000f\nAdded new API for ServiceStates\n\u000f\nClarified shutdown behavior for the\nCommunication Management\n\u000f\nAdded specification of data types\nSampleType and FieldType\n\u000f\nAdded support for MACSec Secure\nCommunication channels\n\u000f\nHarmonization with PRS SOME/IP\nServiceDiscovery Protocol document\n\u000f\nClarified Error codes for Fields, and E2E\nError Handling\n\u000f\nReplaced usage of SamplePtr for\nRawDataStreams\n\u000f\nEditorial changes and bugfixes"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P3_05",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"

      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 3,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "\u000f\nAdded SecOC Behavior, API and\nFreshness Value Management to\nspecification\n\u000f\nStandardized API Error Codes for\nara::com API\n\u000f\nAdded unique ErrorDomain identifiers\n\u000f\nAdded Named Constructor Approach\n\u000f\nUpdated E2E Support for methods and\nevents\n\u000f\nUpdated Raw Data Streaming chapters\n\u000f\nIntroduced optional execution context\nparameter to APIs with an asynchronous\ncallback\n\u000f\nChanged kCapabilityEnforcementError\nto kGrantEnforcementError\n\u000f\nMoved magic numbers for \"entry type\"\nfield to PRS_SOMEIPServiceDiscovery\n\u000f\nEditorial Changes"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P13_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and functional overview\nThis document contains the requirements on the functionality, API and the configura-\ntion of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Communication Management as part of the Adaptive\nAUTOSAR platform foundation.\nThe Communication Management realizes Service Oriented Communication between\nAdaptive AUTOSAR Applications for all levels of communication, e.g. IntraProcess, In-\nterProcess, InterMachine. It consists of potentially generated Service Provider Skele-\ntons and Service Requester Proxies and optionally the generic Communication Man-\nager software for central brokering and configuration.\nThe Communication Management provides a built-in safety mechanism (E2E protec-\ntion), which can be used for all levels of communication for events and methods.\nThe documentation of the Communication Management consists of two documents:\n\u000f\nthe ARAComAPI explanatory document [1], providing explanations of the design\nand behavior descriptions of the ara::com API,\n\u000f\nthis document, providing the requirements on the ara::com API.\nTherefore it is recommended to read the ARAComAPI explanatory document first to\nget an overview and understanding, and to read this document afterward.\n13 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "source_page": 18,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3.2 Related specification\nAUTOSAR provides a General Specification on Basic Software modules [3, RS Gen-\neral], which is also valid for the\nCM\n.\nThus, the specification SWS BSW General shall be considered as additional and re-\nquired specification for\nCM\n.\n18 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P19_22",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_CONSTR_00001",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and assumptions\n4.1 Limitations\nThe current version of this document is missing some functionality which is not stan-\ndardized and specified within the\nSWS Communication Management\ndocument but\ndescribed in\nExplanation of ara::com API\n[1] and implemented in the demonstrator\ncode:\n4.1.1 Local Buffer Overruns\nCurrently it is not specified what happens if local buffers are full because the application\naccesses data slower than they are received over the network.\n4.1.2 SOME/IP\nThe following limitations regarding the SOME/IP functionality described in [4] and [5]\napply:\n4.1.2.1 Optional method arguments with Tag-Length-Value serialization\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00001]\n{DRAFT}\nOptional method arguments with SOME/IP\nTag-Length-Value serialization\nd\nCommunication Management does currently not\nsupport the existence of optional method arguments with the Tag-Length-Value seri-\nalization principle (described in [4] and [5].\nc\n()\n)\n4.1.3 SOME/IP Service Discovery\nThe following limitations regarding the SOME/IP SD functionality described in [6] and\n[5] apply:\n4.1.3.1 SOME/IP Service Discovery Discardable flag\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00002]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Discardable\nflag\nd\nThe specification does not support setting the SOME/IP Service Discovery Dis-\ncardable flag of a SOME/IP entry option to 1 and reacting to the reception of an (un-\nknown/unsupported) option with the Discardable flag set to 1 (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00273], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00275], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00276], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00544]).\nc\n()\n19 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P20_23",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_CONSTR_00003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.1.3.2 SOME/IP Service Discovery Configuration options\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00003]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Configuration\noptions\nd\nThe specification does not support that SOME/IP Service Discovery con-\nfiguration options (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00276] - [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00287]) con-\nfigured via the\nRequiredSomeipServiceInstance\n.\ncapabilityRecord\nrespec-\ntively in the\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\n.\ncapabilityRecord\nand config-\nuration options contained in a FindService respectively OfferService entry of a received\nSOME/IP-SD message are considered during the process of matching offered services\nto required services and vice versa. Any configured and/or received configuration op-\ntions are simply ignored during the matching process, i.e., they don't have any impact\non the result set returned by FindService() or StartFindService(). Please note that the\ntransmission of configuration options is supported.\nc\n()\n4.1.3.3 SOME/IP Service Discovery Load balancing options\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00004]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Load bal-\nancing options\nd\nThe specification does not support that SOME/IP Service Dis-\ncovery load balancing options configured (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00542], [PRS_-\nSOMEIPSD_00544], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00711] - [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00714]) via the\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\n.\nloadBalancingPriority\nand\nProvided-\nSomeipServiceInstance\n.\nloadBalancingWeight\nare included in the OfferSer-\nvice entry of a transmitted SOME/IP-SD message. Additionally, the specification\ndoes not support that load balancing options of an OfferService entry of a received\nSOME/IP-SD message are considered during the process of matching offered ser-\nvices to required services. Any received load balancing options are simply ignored\nduring the matching process, i.e., they don't have any impact on the result set returned\nby FindService() or StartFindService().\nc\n()\n4.1.3.4 SOME/IP Service Discovery SD endpoint options\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00005]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery SD endpoint\noptions\nd\nThe specification does not support that IPv4/IPv6 SD endpoint options (see\n[PRS_SOMEIPSD_00547] - [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00552], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00554]\n- [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00559], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00650], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00651],\n[PRS_SOMEIPSD_00654]) are included in any SOME/IP-SD entry of a transmitted\nSOME/IP-SD message.\nc\n()\n4.1.3.5 SOME/IP Service Discovery Reboot detection\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00006]\n{DRAFT}\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Reboot detec-\ntion\nd\nThe specification does not support SOME/IP Service Discovery reboot detec-\ntion (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00254], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00255], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n20 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P21_24",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_CONSTR_00007",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n00256], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00631], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00258], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_-\n00503], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00449], [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00704]).\nc\n()\n4.1.4 E2E Protection\nThe general limitations regarding E2E protection and the detectable failure modes are\ndescribed in [7]. Additional, platform specific limitations regarding E2E protection are\ndescribed in chapter 7.6.2.1 and 7.6.1.1.\n[SWS_CM_CONSTR_00007]\n{DRAFT}\nE2E Protection\nd\nE2E protection of\nServi-\nceInterface\n.\ntrigger\ns are not supported in the current version of this document.\nc\n()\n4.1.5 Timing of the network behavior\nThe timing of the network behavior is platform vendor specific (examples are: socket\nopen, socket close, trigger to send a find message). This is particularly important\nduring the Functional cluster lifecycle analysis.\n4.2 Applicability to car domains\nNo restrictions to applicability.\n21 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P22_25",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to other functional clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other Functional Clusters in\nthe AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists the interfaces\nprovided by\nCommunication Management\nto other Functional Clusters. Section\n5.2 Required Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nCommunication Manage-\nment\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform is\nprovided in [8].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },
    {

      "source_page": 22,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.1: Interfaces provided by Communication Management to other Functional\nClusters\nFigure 5.1 shows the interfaces provided by\nCommunication Management\nto other\nFunctional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.2: Interfaces required by Communication Management from other Functional\nClusters"

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.3: Interfaces required by Communication Management from other Functional\nClusters\nFigure 5.2 and figure 5.3 show the interfaces required by\nCommunication Manage-\nment\nfrom other Functional Clusters within the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform."

    },

    },

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management\nshould use this interface\nto create and control\nThread\ns used by the\nimplementation."

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5.3 Platform dependencies\nThe Communication Management is dependent on the E2E protection protocol de-\nfined in [9] and [7].     },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P44_126",

      "source_page": 44,
      "category": "architectural_role",

    },
    {

      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00006",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_129",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "4\n[SWS_CM_10336] [SWS_CM_10338]\n[SWS_CM_10339] [SWS_CM_10340]\n[SWS_CM_10341] [SWS_CM_10342]\n[SWS_CM_10343] [SWS_CM_10344]\n[SWS_CM_10345] [SWS_CM_10346]\n[SWS_CM_10347] [SWS_CM_10348]\n[SWS_CM_10349] [SWS_CM_10350]\n[SWS_CM_10362] [SWS_CM_10371]\n[SWS_CM_10414] [SWS_CM_10440]\n[SWS_CM_10441] [SWS_CM_10442]\n[SWS_CM_10443] [SWS_CM_10444]\n[SWS_CM_10447] [SWS_CM_11100]\n[SWS_CM_11101] [SWS_CM_11102]\n[SWS_CM_11103] [SWS_CM_11104]\n[SWS_CM_11105] [SWS_CM_11106]\n[SWS_CM_11107] [SWS_CM_11108]\n[SWS_CM_11109] [SWS_CM_11110]\n[SWS_CM_11111] [SWS_CM_11112]\n[SWS_CM_11144] [SWS_CM_11145]\n[SWS_CM_11146] [SWS_CM_11147]\n[SWS_CM_11148] [SWS_CM_11149]\n[SWS_CM_11150] [SWS_CM_11151]\n[SWS_CM_11152] [SWS_CM_11153]\n[SWS_CM_11154] [SWS_CM_11155]\n[SWS_CM_11156] [SWS_CM_11351]\n[SWS_CM_11353] [SWS_CM_11355]\n[SWS_CM_11357] [SWS_CM_11361]\n[SWS_CM_11363] [SWS_CM_11366]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_130",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide an interface to query the\nresult of an asynchronously called\nservice method"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_131",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00193] [SWS_CM_10362]\n[SWS_CM_10371] [SWS_CM_10440]\n[SWS_CM_11351] [SWS_CM_11353]\n[SWS_CM_11355] [SWS_CM_11357]\n[SWS_CM_11361] [SWS_CM_11363]\n[SWS_CM_11366]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_132",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\ntrigger the application on completion\nof an asynchronously called service\nmethod"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_133",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00197] [SWS_CM_10317]\n[SWS_CM_10318] [SWS_CM_10349]\n[SWS_CM_10350] [SWS_CM_11104]\n[SWS_CM_11108] [SWS_CM_11148]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_134",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide an interface which\naggregates methods to receive a\nnotification on a changed field value\nas well as explicitly getting and\nsetting the field value"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_135",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00008] [SWS_CM_01031]\n[SWS_CM_11403] [SWS_CM_90501]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_136",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide a method to remotely set the\nfield value"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P45_137",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00031] [SWS_CM_00113]\n[SWS_CM_10329] [SWS_CM_10333]\n[SWS_CM_10335] [SWS_CM_10344]\n[SWS_CM_10346] [SWS_CM_10443]\n[SWS_CM_11151] [SWS_CM_11152]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_138",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_139",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide a method to remotely get the\nfield value"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_140",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00014] [SWS_CM_00015]\n[SWS_CM_00016] [SWS_CM_00030]\n[SWS_CM_00112] [SWS_CM_00114]\n[SWS_CM_00115] [SWS_CM_00116]\n[SWS_CM_00117] [SWS_CM_00119]\n[SWS_CM_00120] [SWS_CM_00128]\n[SWS_CM_00129] [SWS_CM_00132]\n[SWS_CM_00133] [SWS_CM_10329]\n[SWS_CM_10333] [SWS_CM_10335]\n[SWS_CM_10344] [SWS_CM_10346]\n[SWS_CM_10412] [SWS_CM_10413]\n[SWS_CM_10415] [SWS_CM_10443]\n[SWS_CM_11151] [SWS_CM_11152]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_141",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide an interface which\naggregates methods to send a\nnotification on value change and to\nregister a get and set function for the\nfield value"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_142",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\ntrigger the set method of the\napplication which provides the field"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_143",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_10338] [SWS_CM_10339]\n[SWS_CM_10340] [SWS_CM_11153]\n[SWS_CM_11154] [SWS_CM_11155]\n[SWS_CM_11156]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_144",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\ntrigger the get method of the\napplication which provides the field"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_145",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_10338] [SWS_CM_10339]\n[SWS_CM_10340] [SWS_CM_11153]\n[SWS_CM_11154] [SWS_CM_11155]\n[SWS_CM_11156]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_146",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The Communication Management\nshall protect the transmission of\nevents using E2E protocol. The E2E\nProtection has to be executed behind\nthe event API."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_147",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00046] [SWS_CM_10473]\n[SWS_CM_90406] [SWS_CM_90430]\n[SWS_CM_90433]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_148",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00042] [SWS_CM_10475]\n[SWS_CM_90407] [SWS_CM_90408]\n[SWS_CM_90412] [SWS_CM_90413]\n[SWS_CM_90417] [SWS_CM_90431]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_149",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprovide an interface to call fire&forget\nservice methods"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_150",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_90434] [SWS_CM_90435]\n[SWS_CM_90436]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_151",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The Communication Management\nshall support a change of the\nconfigured protocol binding without\nrequiring a re-compilation of the\nadaptive application"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_152",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_10384] [SWS_CM_10385]\n[SWS_CM_10386]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_153",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nprotect the transmission of methods\nusing E2E protocol."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P46_154",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00014",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00033] [SWS_CM_00036]\n[SWS_CM_00037] [SWS_CM_00039]\n[SWS_CM_00040] [SWS_CM_00041]\n[SWS_CM_10460] [SWS_CM_10462]\n[SWS_CM_10463] [SWS_CM_10464]\n[SWS_CM_10465] [SWS_CM_10466]\n[SWS_CM_10467] [SWS_CM_10468]\n[SWS_CM_10469] [SWS_CM_10472]\n[SWS_CM_10473] [SWS_CM_90467]\n[SWS_CM_90468] [SWS_CM_90469]\n[SWS_CM_90470] [SWS_CM_90471]\n[SWS_CM_90472] [SWS_CM_90473]\n[SWS_CM_90474] [SWS_CM_90475]\n[SWS_CM_90476] [SWS_CM_90477]\n[SWS_CM_90479] [SWS_CM_90480]\n[SWS_CM_90481] [SWS_CM_90482]\n5"
    },
    {

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },

      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "4\n[SWS_CM_90485] [SWS_CM_90486]\n[SWS_CM_90487] [SWS_CM_90488]\n[SWS_CM_90489] [SWS_CM_90490]\n[SWS_CM_90491] [SWS_CM_90492]\n[SWS_CM_90493] [SWS_CM_90494]\n[SWS_CM_90496] [SWS_CM_90497]\n[SWS_CM_90498]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P47_157",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90485",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_00034] [SWS_CM_00047]\n[SWS_CM_10470] [SWS_CM_10471]\n[SWS_CM_90495] [SWS_CM_90499]"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P47_158",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90485",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Communication Management shall\nsupport a decision for applying the\nmethod call based on E2E results."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P47_159",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90485",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 47,

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P53_204",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10301",

      "source_page": 53,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_01046] [SWS_CM_01050]\n[SWS_CM_01051] [SWS_CM_01052]\n[SWS_CM_01053] [SWS_CM_01054]\n[SWS_CM_01055] [SWS_CM_01056]\n[SWS_CM_01057] [SWS_CM_01058]\n[SWS_CM_01059] [SWS_CM_01060]\n[SWS_CM_01061] [SWS_CM_01062]\n[SWS_CM_01063] [SWS_CM_01064]\n[SWS_CM_01065] [SWS_CM_01066]\n[SWS_CM_01067] [SWS_CM_01068]\n[SWS_CM_01069]"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P53_205",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10301",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 53,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_CM_10445] [SWS_CM_10454]\n[SWS_CM_10455] [SWS_CM_10456]\n[SWS_CM_10457] [SWS_CM_99036]\n[SWS_CM_99037] [SWS_CM_99038]\n[SWS_CM_99039]"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P54_206",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 54,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional specification\n7.1 General description\nThe AUTOSAR Adaptive architecture organizes the software of the AUTOSAR Adap-\ntive foundation as functional clusters. These clusters offer common functionality as\nservices to the applications. The Communication Management (CM) for AUTOSAR\nAdaptive is such a functional cluster and is part of \"AUTOSAR Runtime for Adaptive\nApplications\" - ARA. It is responsible for the construction and supervision of communi-\ncation paths between applications, both local and remote.\nThe CM provides the infrastructure that enables communication between Adaptive\nAUTOSAR Applications within one machine and with software entities on other ma-\nchines, e.g. other Adaptive AUTOSAR applications or Classic AUTOSAR SWCs. All\ncommunication paths can be established at design- , start-up- or run-time.\nThis specification includes the syntax of the API, the relationship of API to the model\nand describes semantics, e.g. through state machines, and assumption of pre-, post-\nconditions and use of APIs. The specification does not provide constraints on the SW\narchitecture of a platform implementation, so there is no definition of basic software\nmodules and no specification of implementation or internal technical architecture of\nthe Communication Management.\n7.1.1 Architectural concepts\nThe Communication management of AUTOSAR Adaptive can be logically divided into\nthe following sub-parts:\n\u000f\nLanguage binding\n\u000f\nEnd-to-end communication protection\n\u000f\nCommunication / Network binding\n\u000f\nCommunication Management software\n54 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P55_207",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P55_208",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.1: Technical Architecture of Communication Management\nIn the context of Communication Management, the following types of interfaces are\ndefined:\n\u000f\nPublic Application Interface: Part of the Adaptive AUTOSAR API and specified in\nthe SWS. This is the standardized ara::com API.\n\u000f\nFunctional Cluster Interactions: Interaction between functional clusters. Not nor-\nmative, intended to make specification more readable and to support integration\nof SW into demonstrator. (dotted arrow in 7.1) And also interactions between\nelements within a functional cluster. Not used in specifications, so it is a non-\nstandardized interface. Used for communication inside Communication Manage-\nment software (grey arrow in 7.1)\nPlease note, that Language Binding and Communication Binding depend on a specific\nconfiguration by the integrator, but they need to be deployed within the application\nbinary. This results in the fact that the serialization of the Communication Binding will\nrun in the execution context of the Adaptive Application.\nFor the design of ARA API the following constraints apply:\n\u000f\nSupport the independence of application software components\n\u000f\nUse of Service-oriented communication without dependency on a specific com-\nmunication protocol\n55 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P56_209",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 56,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nMake the API as lean as possible, neither supporting very specific use cases\nwhich could also be done on top of the API, nor supporting component model\nor higher level concepts. The API is restricted to support core communication\nmechanisms.\n\u000f\nSupport for dynamic communication:\n\nNo discovery by application middleware, the clients know the server but the\nServer does not know the clients. Event subscription is the only dynamic\ncommunication pattern in the application.\n\nFull service discovery in the application. No communication paths are known\nat configuration time. An API for Service discovery allows the application\ncode to choose the service instance.\n\u000f\nSupport both Event/Callback and Polling style usage of the API to enable classic\nRTE style paradigms. To support high determinism demands in case of callback-\nbased / event-based interaction, there shall be the possibility to avoid uncontrolled\ncontext switches.\n\u000f\nSupport both synchronous callback-based communication and asynchronous\ncommunication philosophy.\n\u000f\nSupport of client/server communication.\n\u000f\nSupport of sender/receiver communication with queued semantics where the re-\nceiver caches are configurable.\n\u000f\nSupport of selection of trigger conditions for task activation.\n\u000f\nExtensions for security.\n\u000f\nExtensions for Quality Of Service QoS.\n\u000f\nScalability for real-time systems.\n\u000f\nSupport of built-in end-to-end communication protection, where a use-case-\nspecific behavior can be done on top of ARA API.\n7.1.2 Design decisions\nThe design of the ARA API covers the following principles:\n\u000f\nIt uses the Proxy/Skeleton pattern:\n\nThe (service) proxy is the representative of the possibly remote (i.e. other\nprocess, other core, other node) service. It is an instance of a C++ class\nlocal to the application/client, which uses the service.\n\nThe (service) skeleton is the connection of the user provided service imple-\nmentation to the middleware transport infrastructure. Service implementa-\ntion class is derived from the (service) skeleton.\n56 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P57_210",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\nBeside proxies/skeletons, there might exist a so-called \"Runtime\" (singleton)\nclass to provide some essentials to manage proxies and skeletons. But\nthis is communication management software implementation specific and\ntherefore not specified in this document, but may be specified in a future\nversion.\nRegarding proxy/skeleton design pattern in general and its role in middleware\nimplementations, see [11] [12].\n\u000f\nIt supports callback mechanisms on data reception.\n\u000f\nThe API has zero-copy capabilities including the possibility for memory manage-\nment in the middleware.\n\u000f\nIt is aligned with the AUTOSAR service model (services, instances, events, meth-\nods, ...) to allow the generation of proxies and skeletons out of this model.\n\u000f\nFull discovery and service instance selection support on API level.\n\u000f\nClient/Server Communication uses concepts introduced by C++11 language, e.g.\nstd::future, std::promise, to fully support method calls between different contexts.\n\u000f\nAbstract from SOME/IP specific behavior, but support SOME/IP service mecha-\nnisms, as methods, events and fields.\n\u000f\nSupport/implement the standard end-to-end protection protocols, as specified in\n[9] and [7].\n\u000f\nSupport of Service contract versioning.\n\u000f\nSupport Event and Polling style usage of the API equally to enable classic RT\nstyle paradigms.\n\u000f\nFully exploit C++11/14 features in API design to provide usability and comfort for\nthe application developer.\nSee ARAComAPI explanatory [1] for more details and explanations on the ARA API\ndesign.\n7.1.3 Communication paradigms and Definitions\nService-Oriented Communication (SoC) as a part of Service-Oriented Architecture\n(SOA) [13] is the main communication pattern for Adaptive AUTOSAR Applications.\nIt allows establishing communication paths both at run-time, so it can be used to build\nup dynamic communication with unknown number of participants. Figure 7.2 shows\nthe basic operation principle of Service-Oriented Communication.\n57 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P58_211",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_12002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P58_212",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_12002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: Service-Oriented Communication\nService Discovery decides whether external and internal service-oriented communi-\ncation is established. The discovery strategy shall allow either returning a specific\nservice instance or all available instances providing the requested service at the time\nof the request, no matter if they are available locally or remote. The Communication\nManagement software should provide an optimized implementation for both the Ser-\nvice discovery and the communication connection, depending on the location where\nthe service provider resides. More about Service Discovery can be found in\nSOME/IP\nService Discovery Protocol Specification\n[6].\nThe service class is the central element of the Service-Oriented Communication pat-\ntern applied in Adaptive AUTOSAR. It represents the service by collecting the methods\nand events which are provided or requested by the applications implementing the con-\ncrete service functionality.\n[SWS_CM_12002]\n{DRAFT}\nActive subscriber\nd\nThe active subscriber shall be an\nadaptive application that has invoked the Subscribe method of the respective:\n\u000f\nTrigger class (see [SWS_CM_00723]) or\n\u000f\nField or Event class (see [SWS_CM_00141])\nand has not canceled the subscription by invoking the Unsubscribe method of the re-\nspective:\n\u000f\nTrigger class (see [SWS_CM_00810]) or\n\u000f\nField or Event class (see [SWS_CM_00151])\nc\n(RS_CM_00103, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00120)\n[SWS_CM_12003]\n{DRAFT}\nActive subscriber when SOME/IP Network binding is\nused\nd\nIn addition to [SWS_CM_12002], if SOME/IP Network binding is used to provide\n58 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P59_213",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_00205",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 59,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nservices for an application, the active subscriber shall be an adaptive application for\nwhich the SOME/IP services subscription has not yet expired when the TTL contained\nin the respective SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message has been exceeded (see\n[SWS_CM_00205]).\nc\n(RS_CM_00103, RS_AP_00114, RS_AP_00120)\n7.1.4 Service contract versioning\nIn Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) environments the client and the provider of\na service rely on a contract which covers the service interface and behavior. The\ninterface and the behavior of a service may change over time. Therefore, service\ncontract versioning has been introduced to differentiate between the different versions\nof a service."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P60_214",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P60_215",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99003",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 60,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.4: Service contract versioning flow\nNote:\n1. The contract version of a\nServiceInterface\nconsists of a\nmajorVersion\nand a\nminorVersion\nnumber. The\nmajorVersion\nnumber indicates backwards-\nincompatible service changes. The\nminorVersion\nnumber indicates backwards-\ncompatible service changes.\n\u000f\nfor backwards-incompatible interface or behavior changes the\nmajorVersion\nnumber is increased and the\nminorVersion\nnumber is set to 0.\n\u000f\nfor backwards-compatible interface or behavior changes the\nmajorVersion\nnumber is unchanged and the\nminorVersion\nnumber is increased.\n2. The contract version of a\nServiceInterface\nis mapped to a version of the\nServiceInterfaceDeployment\n. This version mapping may be done several times\nresulting in several\nServiceInterfaceDeployment\ns for the same\nServiceIn-\nterface\n. Such a mapping will result in unambiguous identification on each VLAN\naccording to the [constr_1723] in [5].\n[SWS_CM_99003]\n{DRAFT}\nService interface version evaluation for backwards-\ncompatibility\nd\nThe version of\nServiceInterfaceDeployment\nshall be evaluated\nby the Service Discovery in terms of backwards-compatibility based on the used\nnetwork binding for service connection.\nc\n(RS_CM_00500, RS_CM_00501, RS_CM_-\n00700)\n60 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P61_216",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 61,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2 Communication Group\nNOTE:\nCommunication Groups have been set to obsolete and will be removed or re-\nplaced in the next AUTOSAR release(s).\nThe Communication Group is a communication concept based on\nara::com\nwhich is\ndesigned for Adaptive State Management applications. It can be seen as a composite\nService which manages information routing in a defined manner. A Communication\nGroup has one server and multiple clients. The server is able to send broadcast and\npeer to peer messages to the clients of a Communication Group. The clients can\nacknowledge these messages. The server of a Communication Group can further\nverify how many clients are connected to the Communication Group at every time.\nApplications can connect/disconnect to a Communication Group instance using one of\nthe two Communication Group Service Interfaces,\nCommunicationGroupServer\nor\nCommunicationGroupClient\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P62_217",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99000",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 62,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.1.1 Communication Group Server\n[SWS_CM_99000]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService\nd\nA Com-\nmunication Group shall provide a\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService to be used\nby the Server of a Communication Group.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99001]\n{OBSOLETE}\nBroadcast method of\nCommunication-\nGroupServer\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService shall provide\nthe method\nbroadcast\nto broadcast messages to the clients of the Communication\nGroup. This method shall take as input parameter the\nmessage\nto be broadcasted. In\ncase the\nboardcast\nmethod fails the method return shall provide an error code as\nspecified in [SWS_CM_99024].\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting\nboardcast\nmethod of a generated\nService Proxy/Skeleton interface.\ntemplate <typename T>\nara::core::Future<void> broadcast (const T& msg);\n[SWS_CM_99002]\n{OBSOLETE}\nPeer To Peer Message method of\nCommunica-\ntionGroupServer\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService shall pro-\nvide a method\nmessage\nto send a message to a dedicated client of the Communica-\ntion Group. This method shall take as input parameters the\nmessage\nto be sent, and\nthe\nclientID\nof the client which shall be addressed. In case the\nmessage\nmethod\nfails the method return shall provide an error code as specified in [SWS_CM_99024].\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting\nmessage\nmethod of a generated Ser-\nvice Proxy/Skeleton interface.\ntemplate <typename T>\nara::core::Future<void> message (std::uint32_t clientID, const T& msg);\n[SWS_CM_99014]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMessage Response event of\nCommunication-\nGroupServer\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService shall provide\nan event\nresponse\nthat contains the respond of a dedicated client to a broadcast\nor a peer to peer message of the Communication Group. The event shall provide\nthe\nresponse message\nand the\nclientID\nof this response.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting event\nresponse\nmessage of a gener-\nated Service Proxy/Skeleton interface.\ntemplate <typename R>\nstruct Response {\nstd::uint32_t clientID;\nconst R& responseMsg\n}\n62 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P63_218",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99015",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 63,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_99015]\n{OBSOLETE}\nList Clients method of\nCommunication-\nGroupServer\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService shall provide\na method\nlistClients\nto report about the connected clients of the Communication\nGroup. This method shall have no input parameters and shall return the\nlist of\nclients\n. In case the\nlistClients\nmethod fails the method return shall provide an\nerror code as specified in [SWS_CM_99024].\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting\nlistClients\nmethod of a generated\nService Proxy/Skeleton interface.\nara::core::Future<ara::core::Vector<std::uint32_t>> listClients();\n7.2.1.2 Communication Group Client\n[SWS_CM_99007]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService\nd\nThe\nclients of a Communication Group shall provide a\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService to be used by a Communication Group.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99008]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMessage method of\nCommunicationGroup-\nClient\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService shall provide a\nmethod\nmessage\nfor the client to receive a message from the Communication Group.\nThis method shall take as input parameter the\nmessage\n. In case the\nmessage\nmethod\nfails the method return shall provide an error code as specified in [SWS_CM_99024].\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting\nmessage\nmethod of a generated Ser-\nvice Proxy/Skeleton interface.\ntemplate <typename T>\nara::core::Future<void> message (const T& msg);\n[SWS_CM_99009]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMessage Response event of\nCommunication-\nGroupClient\nService\nd\nThe\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService shall provide\nan event\nresponse\nfor the client to send a response message to the Communication\nGroup. The event shall provide the\nresponse message\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_-\n00601)\nThe C++ signature below presents the resulting event\nresponse\nmessage of a gener-\nated Service Proxy/Skeleton interface.\ntemplate <typename R>\nconst R& responseMsg;\n63 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P64_219",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99010",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 64,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.2 Behavior\nThe Communication Group performs the following tasks to enable a Communication\nGroup.\n[SWS_CM_99010]\n{OBSOLETE}\nBroadcast task\nd\nA Broadcast task shall be triggered\nby the\nbroadcast\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService. The Com-\nmunicationGroup shall forward this broadcast message to all connected clients by call-\ning the\nmessage\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService from each\nconnected client.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99011]\n{OBSOLETE}\nPeer To Peer message task\nd\nA Peer to Peer mes-\nsage task shall be triggered by the\nmessage\nmethod (which includes the client ad-\ndress) of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService. The CommunicationGroup\nshall forward this message to the addressed client by calling the\nmessage\nmethod\nof the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService of this client.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99012]\n{OBSOLETE}\nMessage Response task\nd\nThe Message Response\ntask shall be triggered by the\nmessage response\nevent of the\nCommunication-\nGroupClient\nService from a client . The CommunicationGroup shall forward this\nresponse message with the client source address to the\nmessage response\nevent\nof the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99013]\n{OBSOLETE}\nList Clients task\nd\nThe List Clients task shall be trig-\ngered by the\nlist clients\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService.\nThe CommunicationGroup shall provide the list of all connected client addresses with\nthe return of the\nlist clients\nmethod of the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nSer-\nvice.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n7.2.3 Connection\nThe connection and disconnection to Communication Group is performed by standard\nara::com\nfunctions.\n7.2.3.1 Communication Group Server\nThe Server of a Communication Group connects to a Communication Group by con-\nnecting to the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService of this Communication group\n(using\nFindService\nor\nStartFindService\n).\n[SWS_CM_99016]\n{OBSOLETE}\nConnection Status of a Communication Group\nServer\nd\nThe Server of the Communication Group shall be considered to be connected\nif the server has successfully subscribed to the response\nmessage response\nevent\nof the\nCommunicationGroupServer\nService, else the Server shall be considered\nnot connected.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n64 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P65_220",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 65,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.3.2 Communication Group Client\nA Communication Group client connects to a Communication Group by offering the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService. A Communication Group client disconnects\nto a Communication Group by stop offering the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nSer-\nvice.\n7.2.4 Limitations\nThe Communication Group concept has the following limitations:\n\u000f\nThere is only one Server for an instance of a Communication Group at a given\ntime.\n\u000f\nA Client provides the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nService to only one in-\nstance of a Communication Group at a given time.\nThe figure below outlines a connection example for a Communication Group."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P66_221",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99017",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 66,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_99017]\n{OBSOLETE}\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNICATION_GROUP\nd\nThe\nServiceInterface\n.\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNICATION_GROUP\nshall be used to de-\nfine a Communication Group\ntemplate\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99018]\n{OBSOLETE}\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNICA-\nTION_GROUP_SERVER\nd\nThe\nServiceInterface\n.\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNI-\nCATION_GROUP_SERVER\nshall be used to define\nCommunicationGroupServer\nservice.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99019]\n{OBSOLETE}\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNICA-\nTION_GROUP_CLIENT\nd\nThe\nServiceInterface\n.\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNI-\nCATION_GROUP_CLIENT\nshall be used to define\nCommunicationGroupClient\nservice.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nThe figure below presents the relations between these\ncategory\nvalues."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P66_222",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99017",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 66,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.7: Communication Group service interface categories\n7.2.6 Communication Group Creation\nA Communication Group is created by defining a Communication Group\ntemplate\nonly.\n[SWS_CM_99020]\n{OBSOLETE}\nCommuncation Group\ntemplate\nd\nThe Communi-\ncation Group\ntemplate\nis a\nServiceInterface\nof type\nCommunicationGroup-\nClient\nwith the\ncategory\nvalue\nCOMMUNICATION_GROUP\n. It shall be used to define\na Communication Group, where:\n\u000f\nThe\nSHORT-NAME\nof this\ntemplate\nshall define of the name of the Communica-\ntion Group.\n66 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P67_223",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_99009",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 67,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe event definition according to [SWS_CM_99009] shall define the data type of\nthe\nmessage responses\nof the Communication Group.\n\u000f\nThe method definition according to [SWS_CM_99008] shall define the data type\nof the\nmessages\nof the Communication Group.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_CM_00601)\nBased on the Communication Group\ntemplate\n[SWS_CM_99020] the\nServiceIn-\nterface\ns for the\nCommunicationGroupServer\n[SWS_CM_99000] and the\nCom-\nmunicationGroupClient\n[SWS_CM_99007] can be generated/derived.\n[SWS_CM_99021]\n{OBSOLETE}\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupServer\nservice\nd\nThe\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupServer\nservice shall be the\nSHORT-NAME\nof the according Communi-\ncation Group\ntemplate\nconcatenated by the name\nServer\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\n[SWS_CM_99022]\n{OBSOLETE}\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupClient\nservice\nd\nThe\nSHORT-NAME\nvalue of generated\nCommunica-\ntionGroupClient\nservice shall be the\nSHORT-NAME\nof the according Communi-\ncation Group\ntemplate\nconcatenated by the name\nClient\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00600, RS_-\nCM_00601)\nThe figures below outline the Communication Group creation flow.\nThe Communication Group\nTemplate\ndefines the name of the Communication Group\nand defines the\nmessage\nand\nmessage response\ndatatypes."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P68_224",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 68,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nCommunicationGroupServer\nand the\nCommunicationGroupClient\nSer-\nvice descriptions are derived from the Communication Group\nTemplate\n."
    },
