      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_00196]) shall be made ready according to [SWS_CM_10440].\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_SOMEIP_00008)\n[SWS_CM_10317] Making the Future ready\nd\nIn order to make the\nFuture\nre-\nturned by the function call operator (\noperator()\n) of the respective\nMethod\nclass\n(see [SWS_CM_00196]) ready, depending on the type or received message (see\n[SWS_CM_10357]) either the\nset_value\noperation (see [SWS_CORE_00345] and\n[SWS_CORE_00346]) or the\nSetError\n(see [SWS_CORE_00353]) operation of\nthe\nPromise\ncorresponding to this\nFuture\nshall be invoked. This will unblock\nany blocking\nGet\n,\nwait\n,\nwait_for\n, and\nwait_until\ncalls that have been per-\nformed on this\nFuture\n.  The\nset_value\noperation shall be invoked in case of\na received normal response message using the deserialized payload according to\n[SWS_CM_10316] as an argument. The\nSetError\noperation shall be invoked in case\nof a received error response message using the determined application error accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10358] and [SWS_CM_10429] of type\nara::core::ErrorCode\nas an argument.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215,\nRS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00008)\n[SWS_CM_10318] Invoke the notification function\nd\nIf a notification function has\nbeen registered with the\nFuture\n's\nthen\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00197]), this noti-\nfication function shall be invoked.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nRS_CM_00215, RS_SOMEIP_00007)\n7.4.1.8 Handling Fields\n[SWS_CM_10319] Conditions for sending of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe\nsending of a SOME/IP event message shall be requested in one of the following cases:\n\u000f\nBy invoking the\nUpdate\nmethod of the respective\nField\nclass (see\n[SWS_CM_00119])\n\u000f\nIf the\nFuture\nreturned by the\nSetHandler\nregistered with\nRegister-\nSetHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00116]) becomes ready\nThe SOME/IP event message shall be sent if at least one of the following conditions is\nfulfilled:\n\u000f\nIf there is static service connection according to [SWS_CM_02201] or\n\u000f\nIf there is at least one active subscriber and the offer of the service containing the\nevent has not been stopped (either because the TTL contained in the SOME/IP\nOfferService message (see [SWS_CM_00203]) has expired or because the\nStopOfferService\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00111]) of the\nServiceSkele-\nton\nclass has been called).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00005, RS_SOMEIP_00017, RS_SOMEIP_00018)\n102 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P103_260",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10320",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 103,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10320] Transport protocol for sending of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe SOME/IP event message shall be transmitted using UDP if the threshold defined\nby the\nmulticastThreshold\nattribute of the\nSomeipProvidedEventGroup\nthat\nis aggregated by the\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\nin the role\neventGroup\nin the Manifest has been reached (see [PRS_SOMEIPSD_00134]). The SOME/IP\nevent message shall be transmitted using the transport protocol defined by the\nattribute\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nfieldDeployment\n.\nnotifier\n.\ntransportProtocol\nin the Manifest if this threshold has not been reached (see\n[PRS_SOMEIPSD_00802]).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004,\nRS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00010)\n[SWS_CM_10321] Source of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe source ad-\ndress and the source port of the SOME/IP event message shall set according\nto [SWS_CM_10289].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00042)\n[SWS_CM_10322] Destination of a SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe destination ad-\ndress and the destination port of the SOME/IP event message shall be set according\nto [SWS_CM_10290].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00042)\n[SWS_CM_10323] Content of the SOME/IP event message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP event message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Mani-\nfest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\neventDeployment\n.\neventId\nby adding 0x8000 to the\neventDeployment\n.\neventId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) is unused for event messages (ac-\ncording to [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) and thus shall be set to 0x0000.\n\u000f\nIn case of inactive Session Handling, see [SWS_CM_10240], the Session ID (see\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) is unused for event messages and thus shall be set to\n0x0000 (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00932]) and [PRS_SOMEIP_00925]).\nIn case of active Session Handling, see [SWS_CM_10240], the Session ID\nis used for event messages and thus shall be incremented (with proper wrap\naround) upon every transmission of an event message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00933], [PRS_SOMEIP_00934], [PRS_SOMEIP_00521], and [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00925]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n103 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P104_261",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10324",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 104,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nNOTIFICATION\n(0x02).\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) is\nunused for event messages and thus (according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00925]) shall\nbe set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload shall contain the serialized payload (i.e., the serialized\nField\ncom-\nposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nfield\n) according to the SOME/IP\nserialization rules.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00041, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00022, RS_SOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10324] Checks for a received SOME/IP event message\nd\nUpon reception\nof a SOME/IP event message the checks defined in [SWS_CM_10292] shall be con-\nducted. If any of the above checks fails the received SOME/IP event message shall be\ndiscarded and and the incident shall be logged (if logging is enabled for the\nara::\ncom\nimplementation).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00019, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00022, RS_SOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009,\nRS_SOMEIP_00014)\n[SWS_CM_10325] Identifying the right event\nd\nUsing the Service ID (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInterfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServi-\nceInterfaceDeployment\nelement as well as the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00245]) and 0x8000 + the\neventId\nattribute of the\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nnotifier\ns of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n, the right event shall\nbe identified.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004,\nRS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00022)\n[SWS_CM_10380] Silently discarding SOME/IP event messages for unsubscribed\nevents\nd\nIf the event identified according to [SWS_CM_10325] does not have an active\nsubscription because the\nSubscribe\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00141]) of the specific\nField\nclass of the\nServiceProxy\nclass has not been called, or the\nUnsubscribe\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00151]) of the specific\nField\nclass of the\nServiceProxy\nclass has been called, or the TTL of the SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup message\n(see [SWS_CM_00205]) has expired, the received SOME/IP event message shall be\nsilently discarded (i.e., [SWS_CM_10326], [SWS_CM_10327], and [SWS_CM_10328]\nshall\nnot\nbe performed).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00203, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10328] Invoke receive handler\nd\nIn case a\nReceiveHandler\nwas reg-\nistered using the\nSetReceiveHandler\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00181]) of the re-\nspective\nField\nclass for the event determined according to [SWS_CM_10325] this\n104 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P105_262",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10326",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 105,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nregistered receive handler shall be invoked.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00203, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10326] Deserializing the payload\nd\nBased on the event determined ac-\ncording to [SWS_CM_10325] the Payload of the SOME/IP event message (i.e., the se-\nrialized\nField\ncomposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nfield\n) shall be deseri-\nalized according to the SOME/IP serialization rules.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00028)\nThe SOME/IP seri-\nalization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10327] Providing the received event data\nd\nThe deserialized pay-\nload containing the event data shall be provided via the\nGetNewSamples\n(see\n[SWS_CM_00701]) method of the respective\nField\nclass for the event determined\naccording to [SWS_CM_10325].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00004, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10329] Conditions for sending of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe\nsending of a SOME/IP request message shall be requested by invoking the\nSet\nor\nGet\nmethod of the respective\nField\nclass (see [SWS_CM_00112] and [SWS_CM_00113])\nif the providing service instance has not stopped offering the service (either because\nthe TTL contained in the SOME/IP OfferService message (see [SWS_CM_00203]) has\nexpired or because the\nStopOfferService\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00111]) of the\nServiceSkeleton\nclass has been called).\nc\n(RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nCM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10443] Failures in sending of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nIf the\nsending of the SOME/IP request message fails locally (in a way which is notified\nto the\nara::com\nimplementation), the\nara::com\nimplementation shall make the\nFuture\nreturned by the\nSet\nor\nGet\nmethod of the respective\nField\nclass (see\n[SWS_CM_00112] and [SWS_CM_00113]) ready according to [SWS_CM_10440].\nc\n(RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10330] Transport protocol for sending of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe SOME/IP request message for the\nSet\nmethod shall be transmitted using the\ntransport protocol defined by the attribute\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nfieldDeployment\n.\nset\n.\ntransportProtocol\nin the Manifest. The SOME/IP re-\nquest message for the\nGet\nmethod shall be transmitted using the transport protocol de-\nfined by the attribute\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nfieldDeployment\n.\nget\n.\ntransportProtocol\nrespectively.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_-\n00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00010)\n[SWS_CM_10331] Source of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe source ad-\ndress and the source port of the SOME/IP request message shall be set accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10299].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00010)\n105 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P106_263",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10332",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 106,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10332] Destination of a SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe destination ad-\ndress and the destination port of the SOME/IP request message shall be set accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10300].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10333] Content of the SOME/IP request message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP request message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) for the\nSet\nmethod shall be derived\nfrom the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement\ndefines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nset\n.\nmethodId\n. The Method ID for the\nGet\nmethod shall be derived from the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nget\n.\nmethodId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) shall be set to a value that uniquely\nidentifies the client within a\nMachine\n.  This may be achieved by dynamically\ngenerating unique client IDs upon construction of the\nServiceProxy\n.\n\u000f\nThe Session ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) shall be set to 0x0001 for the first\ncall of the particular method by a given client and shall be incremented by 1\nafter each call performed by this client for the respective method (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00533]). Once the Session ID reaches 0xFFFF, it shall wrap around\nand start with 0x0001 again (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00521]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) is\nunused for request messages and thus (according to [PRS_SOMEIP_00920])\nshall be set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload for the request message for the\nSet\nmethod shall contain the seri-\nalized payload (i.e., the serialized\nField\ncomposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nfield\n) according to the SOME/IP serialization rules. The Payload for the\nrequest message for the\nGet\nmethod will be empty.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_00003,\n106 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P107_264",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 107,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nRS_SOMEIP_00012, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00025, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00041)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10334] Checks for a received SOME/IP request message\nd\nUpon recep-\ntion of a SOME/IP request message the following checks shall be conducted:\n\u000f\nVerify that the Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) is set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) is larger than 7.\n\u000f\nUse the Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) which is set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00) to determine that the received SOME/IP message is actually a SOME/IP\nrequest message.\n\u000f\nUse the Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInter-\nfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement in\nthe Manifest to determine the right\nServiceInterface\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) matches the\nmetho-\ndId\nattribute of one of the\nSomeipMethodDeployment\ns of the\nSomeipSer-\nviceInterfaceDeployment\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) is set to\nREQUEST\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nVerify that the Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) matches\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n.\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nVerify that the Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00191]) is set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\nIf any of the above checks fails the received SOME/IP request mes-\nsage shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is\nenabled for the\nara::com\nimplementation). In case of a received RE-\nQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR\nmessage with return code set to either\nE_WRONG_PROTOCOL_VERSION\n,\nE_UNKNOWN_SERVICE\n,\nE_WRONG_INTERFACE_VERSION\n,\nE_UNKNOWN_METHOD\n,\nor\nE_WRONG_MESSAGE_TYPE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the\nrequester, depending on the detected error.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200,\nRS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_00019, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00008,\nRS_SOMEIP_00014)\n[SWS_CM_10335] Identifying the right method\nd\nUsing the Service ID (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInterfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServi-\nceInterfaceDeployment\nelement as well as the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00245]) and the\nmethodId\nattribute of the\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nset\ns and\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nget\ns of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n,\n107 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P108_265",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 108,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthe right method shall be identified.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00021)\n[SWS_CM_10336] Deserializing the payload\nd\nBased on the method determined ac-\ncording to [SWS_CM_10335] the Payload of the SOME/IP request message shall be\ndeserialized according to the SOME/IP serialization rules.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00028)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10338] Invoke the registered set/get handlers - event driven\nd\nIn case\na\nMethodCallProcessingMode\nof either\nkEvent\nor\nkEventSingleThread\nhas\nbeen passed to the constructor of the\nServiceSkeleton\n(see [SWS_CM_00130]),\nthe deserialized payload containing the method data (i.e., method ID and input ar-\nguments) shall be used to invoke a registered\nSetHandler\nresp.\nGetHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00114] and [SWS_CM_00116]) of the\nField\nclass as a conse-\nquence to the reception of the SOME/IP request message.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220, RS_CM_00221, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10339] Invoke the registered set/get handlers - polling\nd\nIn case a\nMethodCallProcessingMode\nof\nkPoll\nhas been passed to the constructor of\nthe\nServiceSkeleton\n(see [SWS_CM_00130]), the deserialized payload contain-\ning the method data (i.e., method ID and input arguments) shall be used to in-\nvoke a registered\nSetHandler\nresp.\nGetHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00114] and\n[SWS_CM_00116]) of the\nField\nclass upon a call to the\nProcessNextMethodCall\nmethod (see [SWS_CM_00199]) of the\nServiceSkeleton\nclass.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220, RS_CM_00221, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10340] Conditions for sending of a SOME/IP response message\nd\nThe sending of a SOME/IP response message shall be requested upon the re-\nturn of a registered\nSetHandler\nresp.\nGetHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00114]\nand [SWS_CM_00116]).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nCM_00220, RS_CM_00221, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10341] Transport protocol for sending of a SOME/IP response mes-\nsage\nd\nThe SOME/IP response message for the\nSet\nmethod shall be transmit-\nted using the transport protocol defined by the attribute\nSomeipServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\n.\nfieldDeployment\n.\nset\n.\ntransportProtocol\nin the Manifest.\nThe SOME/IP response message for the\nGet\nmethod shall be transmitted using\nthe transport protocol defined by the attribute\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeploy-\nment\n.\nfieldDeployment\n.\nget\n.\ntransportProtocol\nrespectively.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00010)\n108 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P109_266",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10342",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 109,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10342] Source of a SOME/IP response message\nd\nThe source ad-\ndress and the source port of the SOME/IP response message shall be set accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10310].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00010)\n[SWS_CM_10343] Destination of a SOME/IP response message\nd\nThe destination\naddress and the destination port of the SOME/IP response message shall be set\naccording to [SWS_CM_10311].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nRS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10344] Content of the SOME/IP response message\nd\nThe entries in the\nSOME/IP response message shall be as follows:\n\u000f\nThe Service ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) shall be derived from the Manifest\nwhere the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nser-\nviceInterfaceId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00245]) for the\nSet\nmethod shall be derived\nfrom the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement\ndefines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nset\n.\nmethodId\n. The Method ID for the\nGet\nmethod shall be derived from the Manifest where the\nSomeipServiceInter-\nfaceDeployment\nelement defines the\nfieldDeployment\n.\nget\n.\nmethodId\n.\n\u000f\nThe Length (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00042]) shall be set to the length of the seri-\nalized payload in units of bytes incremented by 8 (second part of the SOME/IP\nheader that is covered by the Length)\n\u000f\nThe Client ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00702]) shall be copied from the correspond-\ning SOME/IP request message (see [SWS_CM_10301]).\n\u000f\nThe Session ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00703]) shall be copied from the corre-\nsponding SOME/IP request message (see [SWS_CM_10301]).\n\u000f\nThe Protocol Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00052]) shall be set to 0x01.\n\u000f\nThe Interface Version (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00053]) shall be derived from the\nManifest where the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nelement defines\nthe\nserviceInterfaceVersion\n.\nmajorVersion\n.\n\u000f\nThe Message Type (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]) shall be set to\nRESPONSE\n(0x80).\n\u000f\nThe Return Code (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00058] and [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall\nbe set to\nE_OK\n(0x00).\n\u000f\nThe Payload shall contain the serialized payload (i.e., the serialized\nField\ncom-\nposed by the\nServiceInterface\nin role\nfield\n) which has either been pro-\nvided by the value of the\nFuture\nreturned by the registered\nSetHandler\nresp.\nGetHandler\nor obtained internally) according to the SOME/IP serialization rules.\n109 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218,\nRS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00003, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00012, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00025, RS_SOMEIP_00041, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00008)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10345] Checks for a received SOME/IP response message\nd\nUpon re-\nception of a SOME/IP response message the checks defined in [SWS_CM_10313]\nshall be conducted. If any of the above checks fails the received SOME/IP event\nmessage shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is en-\nabled for the\nara::com\nimplementation).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_-\nCM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00003, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00012, RS_SOMEIP_00019, RS_SOMEIP_00021, RS_SOMEIP_00025,\nRS_SOMEIP_00041, RS_SOMEIP_00008, RS_SOMEIP_00014)\n[SWS_CM_10346] Identifying the right method\nd\nUsing the Service ID (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00245]) and the\nserviceInterfaceId\nattribute of the\nSomeipServi-\nceInterfaceDeployment\nelement as well as the Method ID (see [PRS_SOMEIP_-\n00245]) and the\nmethodId\nattribute of the\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nset\ns and\nSomeipFieldDeployment\n.\nget\ns of the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\n,\nthe right method shall be identified.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00021)\n[SWS_CM_10347] Discarding orphaned responses\nd\nOrphaned responses shall\nbe discarded according to [SWS_CM_10315].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_-\nCM_00213)\n[SWS_CM_10348] Deserializing the payload\nd\nBased on the method determined ac-\ncording to [SWS_CM_10346] the Payload of the SOME/IP response message shall be\ndeserialized according to the SOME/IP serialization rules.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00028)\nThe SOME/IP serialization rules are explained in section 7.4.1.9.\n[SWS_CM_10444] Failures during deserialization of response messages\nd\nIn\ncase of failures during deserialization of response messages, the\nara::com\nimple-\nmentation shall make the\nFuture\nreturned by the\nSet\nor\nGet\nmethod of the re-\nspective\nField\nclass (see [SWS_CM_00112] and [SWS_CM_00113]) ready accord-\ning to [SWS_CM_10440].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_-\nSOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009, RS_SOMEIP_00028)\n[SWS_CM_10349] Making the Future ready\nd\nIn order to make the\nFuture\nreturned\nby the\nSet\nor\nGet\nmethod of the respective\nField\nclass (see [SWS_CM_00113] and\n[SWS_CM_00112]) ready, the\nset_value\noperation (see [SWS_CORE_00345] and\n[SWS_CORE_00346]) of the\nPromise\ncorresponding to this\nFuture\nshall be invoked\nusing the deserialized payload as an argument. This will unblock any blocking\nGet\n,\nwait\n,\nwait_for\n, and\nwait_until\ncalls that have been performed on this\nFuture\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215, RS_SOMEIP_-\n00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n110 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10350] Invoke the notification function\nd\nAny registered notification func-\ntion shall be invoked according to [SWS_CM_10318].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215, RS_SOMEIP_00007, RS_SOMEIP_00009)\n[SWS_CM_10363]\n{DRAFT}\nFailures in sending a SOME/IP event message\nd\nIf the\nsending of the\nSOME/IP\nevent message generated by a field update fails locally (due to\na network error which is notified to the ara::com implementation), the\nara::com\nimple-\nmentation shall return an error indicating \"network binding failure\" in the Result of the\nUpdate()\nmethod of the respective Field class (see [SWS_CM_00119]).\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00005, RS_CM_00004)\n7.4.1.9 Serialization of Payload\n[SWS_CM_10034] Serialization of Payload\nd\nThe serialization of the payload shall\nbe based on the definition of the\nServiceInterface\nof the data.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00201, RS_SOMEIP_00004, RS_SOMEIP_00005, RS_SOMEIP_00028)\n[SWS_CM_10169] Missing parameters\nd\nTo allow migration the deserialization shall\nignore parameters attached to the end of previously known parameter list.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00202)\nThis means: Parameters that were not defined in the\nServiceInterface\nused to\ngenerate or parametrize the deserialization code but exist at the end of the serialized\ndata will be ignored by the deserialization.\n[SWS_CM_10259] Seralization Padding\nd\nAfter the serialized data of a variable data\nlength\nDataPrototype\na padding for alignment purposes shall be added for the con-\nfigured alignment (see [SWS_CM_10260]) if the variable data length\nDataPrototype\nis not the last element in the serialized data stream.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nThis requirement does not apply for the serialization\nof extensible structs and methods (see chapter 7.4.1.9.3).\n[SWS_CM_10260] Setting the alignment for a variable data length data el-\nement\nd\nIf\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransforma-\ntionProps\n.\nalignment\nis set for a variable data length data element, the\nvalue of\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransforma-\ntionProps\n.\nalignment\nshall define the alignment. This requirement does not ap-\nply for the serialization of extensible structs and methods.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n(see chapter 7.4.1.9.3)\n[SWS_CM_11262] Missing alignment for a variable data length data ele-\nment\nd\nIf\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransforma-\ntionProps\n.\nalignment\nis not set for a variable data length data element, the value\nof\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nalignment\nshall define the alignment. This requirement does not\napply for the serialization of extensible structs and methods.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n(see chapter 7.4.1.9.3)\n111 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P112_269",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11263",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 112,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11263] Precedence of alignment settings for a variable data length\ndata element\nd\nIf\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nalignment\nand\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nalignment\nare both not set for a\nvariable data length data element, no alignment shall be applied.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10263] Padding for a fixed length data element\nd\nAfter serialized fixed\ndata length data elements, the SOME/IP network binding shall never add automatically\na padding for alignment.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00211)\nNote:\nIf the following data element shall be aligned, a padding element of according size\nneeds to be explicitly inserted into the\nCppImplementationDataType\n.\n[SWS_CM_10037] Alignment calculation\nd\nAlignment shall always be calculated from\nstart of SOME/IP message.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_-\nCM_00211)\nThis attribute defines the memory alignment. The SOME/IP network binding does not\ntry to automatically align parameters but aligns as specified. The alignment is currently\nconstraint to multiple of 1 Byte to simplify code generators.\nSOME/IP payload should be placed in memory so that the SOME/IP payload is suit-\nable aligned. For infotainment ECUs an alignment of 8 Bytes (i.e. 64 bits) should be\nachieved, for all ECU at least an alignment of 4 Bytes should be achieved. An efficient\nalignment is highly hardware dependent.\n[SWS_CM_10016] Deserializing of exceeded unexpected data\nd\nIf more data than\nexpected shall be deserialized, the unexpected data shall be discarded. The known\nfraction shall be considered.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_11411] Deserializing incomplete data on the skeleton side\nd\nIf less\ndata than expected shall be deserialized on the skeleton side the data shall be dis-\ncarded and the incident shall be logged. In case of a received REQUEST mes-\nsage (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR message with return code\nset to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the re-\nquester.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_11412] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side\nd\nIf less data\nthan expected shall be deserialized on the proxy side and the data to be deserialized\ndoes not belong to a Field or Event, the data shall be discarded and the incident shall\nbe logged. In case of a received REQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]),\nadditionally, an ERROR message with return code set to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the requester.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_10017] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side belonging to\na field and initValue defined\nd\nIf less data than expected shall be deserialized on the\nproxy side and the data to be deserialized belong to a\nField\nand the\ninitValue\nis\n112 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "source_page": 113,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\ndefined, the\ninitValue\nshall be used as a substitute for the missing data.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_11413] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side belonging to\na field and initValue not defined\nd\nIf less data than expected shall be deserialized\non the proxy side and the data to be deserialized belong to a\nField\nand the\ninit-\nValue\nis not defined the data shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged.\nIn case of a received REQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally,\nan ERROR message with return code set to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the requester.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_12004] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side belonging to\nan event and\neventReceptionDefaultValue\nis defined\nd\nIf less data than ex-\npected shall be deserialized on the proxy side and the data to be deserialized be-\nlongs to an Event and the\neventReceptionDefaultValue\nis defined, then the\neventReceptionDefaultValue\nshall be used as a substitute for the missing data.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\n[SWS_CM_12005] Deserializing incomplete data on the proxy side belonging to\nan event and\neventReceptionDefaultValue\nis not defined\nd\nIf less data than ex-\npected shall be deserialized on the proxy side and the data to be deserialized belongs\nto an Event and the\neventReceptionDefaultValue\nis not defined, then the data\nshall be discarded and the incident shall be logged.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00202)\nIn the following the serialization of different parameters is specified.\n7.4.1.9.1 Basic Data Types\n[SWS_CM_10036] Serialization of supported primitive\nStdCppImplementation-\nDataType\ns\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P114_271",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10361",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: Primitive\nStdCppImplementationDataType\ns defined in [14].\nThe Byte Order is specified common for all parameters by\nbyteOrder\nof\nApSomeip-\nTransformationProps\n.\n7.4.1.9.2 Enumeration Data Types\n[SWS_CM_10361] Serializing Enumeration Data Type\nd\nEnumeration Data\nType\nshall be serialized according to [SWS_CM_10036] based on their underlying\nprimitive\nStdCppImplementationDataType\n(i.e., the\nPrimitive Cpp Imple-\nmentation Data Type\nthat is defined as the underlying type of the enumeration\nas defined in [SWS_LBAP_00027])\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n7.4.1.9.3 Structured Data Types (structs)\n[SWS_CM_10042] Serializing a struct Data Type\nd\nA\nStructure Cpp Implemen-\ntation Data Type\nshall be serialized in order of depth-first traversal.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nThe SOME/IP network binding doesn't automatically align parameters of a struct.\nInsert reserved/padding elements into the AUTOSAR data type if needed for alignment,\nsince the SOME/IP network binding shall not automatically add such padding.\nSo if for example a struct includes a std::uint8_t and a std::uint32_t, they are just written\nsequentially into the buffer. This means that there is no padding between the uint8\nand the first byte of the std::uint32_t; therefore, the std::uint32_t might not be aligned.\nSo the system designer has to consider to add padding elements to the data type to\nachieve the required alignment or set it globally.\nWarning about unaligned structs or similar shall not be done in the SOME/IP network\nbinding but only in the tool chain used to generate the SOME/IP network binding.\nThe SOME/IP network binding does not automatically insert dummy/padding elements.\nSOME/IP allows to add a length field of 8, 16 or 32 bit in front of structs. The length\nfield of a struct describes the number of bytes of the struct. This allows for extensible\nstructs which allow better migration of interfaces.\n[SWS_CM_00252] Missing size of length field for structs\nd\nIf attribute\nSomeip-\nDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsize-\nOfStructLengthField\nis set to a value equal to 0, no length field shall be inserted\nin front of the serialized struct for which the\nApSomeipTransformationProps\nis\ndefined via\nSomeipDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n114 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_00254] Precedence when setting size of length field for structs\nd\nIf at-\ntribute\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntrans-\nformationProps\n.\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nis set to a value greater 0\nand       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_00255] Default size of length field for structs\nd\nIf attribute\nTrans-\nformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformation-\nProps\n.\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nis not set and attribute\nSomeipDataPro-\ntotypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsizeOf-\nStructLengthField\nis not set, no length field shall be inserted in front of the\nserialized struct.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10270] Default byte order for the length field of structs\nd\nIf at-\ntribute\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntrans-\nformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis not set and attribute\nSomeipDataPrototype-\nTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis not set, a\nbyte order of\nmostSignificantByteFirst\n(i.e., big endian) shall be used for the\nlength field that shall be inserted in front of the serialized associative struct.\nc\n(RS_-\nCM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10253] Default data type for the length field of structs\nd\nIf\nSomeip-\nDataPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsize-\nOfStructLengthField\ndefines the data type for the length field of a struct, the data\nshall be:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_00256] Default data type for the length field of structs\nd\nIf\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nsizeOfStructLengthField\ndefines the the data type for the length\nfield of a struct, the data shall be:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfStructLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10218] Scope of length field value for structs\nd\nThe serializing SOME/IP\nnetwork binding shall write the size (in bytes) of the serialized struct (without the size\nof the length field) into the length field of the struct.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10219] Length greater than expected struct length\nd\nIf the length is\ngreater than the expected length of a struct (as specified in the data type definition) a\ndeserializing SOME/IP network binding shall only interpret the expected data and skip\nthe unexpected.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n116 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo determine the start of the next expected data following the skipped unexpected part,\nthe SOME/IP network binding can use the supplied length information."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P117_275",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_01046",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 117,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.13: Serialization of Structs with Length Fields (Example)\n[SWS_CM_01046] Definition of\ntlvDataIdDefinition\nd\nRegarding the definition\nof\ntlvDataIdDefinition\nsee [TPS_MANI_01097] and [constr_1594] for details.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00205, RS_SOMEIP_00050)\n117 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P118_276",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90443",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 118,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.1.9.4 Structured Datatypes and Arguments with Identifier and optional\nMembers\nTo achieve enhanced forward and backward compatibility, an additional Data ID can\nbe added in front of struct members or method arguments. The receiver then can\nskip unknown members/arguments, i.e. where the Data ID is unknown. New member-\ns/arguments can be added at arbitrary positions when Data IDs are transferred in the\nserialized byte stream.\nStructs are modeled in the Manifest using\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory\nSTRUCTURE\nand members are represented by\nCppImplementation-\nDataTypeElement\ns. Method arguments are represented by ArgumentDataProto-\ntypes.\nThe assignment of Data IDs is modeled in the Manifest in the context of\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n. Refer to [5] for more details.\nMoreover, the usage of Data IDs allows describing structs with optional members.\nWhether a member is optional or not, is defined in the Manifest using the attribute\nCppImplementationDataTypeElement\n.\nisOptional\n.\nWhether an optional member is actually present in the struct or not, is to be determined\nduring runtime. This is realized in the Adaptive Platform using the\nara::core::\nOptional\nclass template (see 8.1.2.6.3 Optional Data Types).\nIn addition to the Data ID, a wire type encodes the datatype of the following member.\nData ID and wire type are encoded in a so-called tag.\nFor more details, please refer to [4].\n[SWS_CM_90443] Wire type for non-dynamic data types\nd\nIf\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynamicLengthFieldSize\nis set to false or is not defined, the serializer\nshall use wire type 4 for serializing complex types and shall use the fixed size\nlength fields. The size is defined in\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfStructLengthField\n,\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nor\nsizeOfStringLengthField\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90444] Wire type for dynamic data types\nd\nIf\nTransformationProp-\nsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynami-\ncLengthFieldSize\nis set to true, the transformer shall use wire types 5,6,7 for\nserializing complex types and shall chose the size of the length field according to this\nwire type.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90445] A deserializer shall always be able to handle the wire types\n4, 5, 6 and 7\nd\nA deserializer shall always be able to handle the wire types 4, 5, 6\nand 7 independent of the setting of\nTransformationPropsToServiceInter-\nfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nisDynamicLengthFieldSize\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n118 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P119_277",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90446",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 119,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_90446] Data ID\nd\nIf a Data ID is defined for an\nArgumentDataPrototype\nor\nCppImplementationDataType\nby means of\nTransformationPropsToSer-\nviceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\nTlvDataIdDefinition\n.\nid\n, a tag shall be in-\nserted in the serialized byte stream.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nNote: regarding existence of Data IDs, refer to [5].\nNote: regarding existence of length field, refer to [4].\nRationale: The length field is required to skip unknown members/arguments during\ndeserialization.\n[SWS_CM_90451] Byte order for the length field of serialized structs\nd\nTransfor-\nmationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nshall define the byte order for the length field.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\n[SWS_CM_90452] Default byte order for the length field of structs\nd\nIf\nTransformationPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransfor-\nmationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis not defined, a byte order of mostSignificantByteFirst\nshall be used for the length field.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nRegarding structure members and serialization examples, refer to [4].\n7.4.1.9.5 Strings\n[SWS_CM_10053] Strings encoding\nd\nStrings shall be encoded using Unicode and\nterminated with a \"\\0\"-character.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10054] Supported encoding\nd\nDifferent Unicode encoding shall be sup-\nported including UTF-8, UTF-16BE, and UTF-16LE. Since these encoding have a dy-\nnamic length of bytes per character, the maximum length in bytes is up to three times\nthe length of characters in UTF-8 plus 1 Byte for the termination with a \"\\0\" or two\ntimes the length of the characters in UTF-16 plus 2 Bytes for a \"\\0\". UTF-8 character\ncan be up to 6 bytes and an UTF-16 character can be up to 4 bytes.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204,\nRS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n[SWS_CM_10285] Responsibility of proper string encoding\nd\nThe application pro-\nvides the string always in the UTF-8 encoding. The SOME/IP binding has to re-\nencode the data to the on-the-wire encoding that is configured by\nApSomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nstringEncoding\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_-\n00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n[SWS_CM_10055] UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE terminating bytes\nd\nUTF-16LE and\nUTF-16BE strings shall be zero terminated with a \"\\0\" character. This means they shall\nend with (at least) two 0x00 Bytes.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n119 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P120_278",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10056",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 120,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10056] UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE strings length\nd\nUTF-16LE and UTF-\n16BE strings shall have an even length.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_-\n00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10057] Odd UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE string length\nd\nFor UTF-16LE and\nUTF-16BE strings having an odd length the last byte shall be silently removed by the re-\nceiving SOME/IP network binding.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10248] Odd UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE string length\nd\nIn case of UTF-\n16LE and UTF-16BE strings having an odd length, after removal of the last byte, the\ntwo bytes before shall be 0x00 bytes (termination) for a string to be valid.\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10058] String start byte(BOM)\nd\nAll strings shall always start with a\nByte Order Mark (BOM).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_-\n00211)\nFor the specification of BOM, see [15] and [16]. Please note that the BOM is used in\nthe serialized strings to achieve compatibility with Unicode.\n[SWS_CM_10459]\n{OBSOLETE}\nLegacy string serialization\nd\nThe legacy string\nserialization shall be triggered if a Unicode is detected and attribute\nAp-\nSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nimplementsLegacyStringSerialization\nis\ntrue.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10059] BOM checking by SOME/IP network binding implementation\nd\nThe receiving SOME/IP network binding implementation shall check the BOM and\nhandle a missing BOM or a malformed BOM as an error by discarding the complete\npayload and logging the incident (if logging is enabled for the ara::com implementa-\ntion).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10060] BOM addition\nd\nThe BOM shall be added by the SOME/IP sending\nnetwork binding implementation.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10061] Supported encoding of CppImplementationDataType with cat-\negory equal to STRING\nd\nIf a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith category equal\nto STRING is used in the context of a\nServiceInterface\nthen the encoding of this\nString DataType is UTF-8.\nc\n()\nThis means that the\nCppImplementationDataType\ncan only be mapped to an\nAp-\nplicationDataType\nof category STRING where attribute\nswDataDefProps\n.\nsw-\nTextProps\n.\nbaseType\n.\nbaseTypeEncoding\nis set to the value UTF-8 as defined\nby [constr_5035]. If a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwithout an\nApplication-\nDataType\nis used there is no formal description about the UTF-8 encoding in the\nServiceInterface\ndescription.\nAccording to SOME/IP serialized strings start with a length field of 8, 16 or 32 bit which\npreceeds the actual string data. The value of this length field holds the length of the\nstring including the BOM and any string termination in units of bytes.\n120 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nlength field that shall be inserted in front of the serialized string.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10277] Data type of the length field for strings\nd\nIf\nSomeipDat-\naPrototypeTransformationProps\n.\nsomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsizeOf-\nStringLengthField\ndefines the the data type for the length field of a string, the\ndata shall be:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10278] Data type of the length field for strings\nd\nIf\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfStringLengthField\ndefines the the data type for the length field of a string,\nthe data shall be:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfStringLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10245] Serialization of strings\nd\nSerialization of strings shall consist of the\nfollowing steps:\n1. Add the Length Field - The value of the length field shall be filled with the number\nof bytes needed for the string (i.e., the result of\nara::core::String::length\n()\n), including the BOM and any string termination that needs to be added.\n2. Appending BOM right after the length field according to the configured\nAp-\nSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\n, if BOM is not already available\nin the first 3 (UTF-8) bytes of the to be serialized array containing the string. If\nthe BOM is already present, simply copy the BOM into the output buffer.\n3. Perform the re-encoding from UTF-8 to UTF-16 if the on-the-wire encoding is\nconfigured as UTF-16 by\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nstringEncod-\ning\n. The re-encoding from UTF-8 to UTF-16BE shall be done if the configured\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis set to\nmostSignificant-\nByteFirst\n. The re-encoding rom UTF-8 to to UTF-16LE shall be done if the\nconfigured\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis set to\nmostSig-\nnificantByteLast\n.\n4. Copying the string data into the output buffer.\n5. Termination of the string with\n0x00\n(UTF-8) or\n0x0000\n(UTF-16) if not terminated\nyet by appending\n0x00\n(UTF-8) or\n0x0000\n(UTF-16).\n122 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n[SWS_CM_10247]\n{DRAFT}\nDeserialization of strings\nd\nDeserialization of strings\nshall consist of the following steps:\n1. Check whether the string starts with a BOM. If not, the complete payload shall\nbe discarded and the incident shall be logged (if logging is enabled for the\nara::com implementation). In case of a received REQUEST message (see\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR message with return code set\nto\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the\nrequester.\n2. Check whether BOM has the same value as\nApSomeipTransformation-\nProps\n.\nbyteOrder\n. If not, the complete payload shall be discarded and the\nincident shall be logged. In case of a received REQUEST message (see [PRS_-\nSOMEIP_00055]), additionally, an ERROR message with return code set to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n(see [PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the re-\nquester.\n3. Remove the BOM\n4. Silently discard the last byte of the string in case of an UTF-16 string with odd\nlength (in bytes)\n5. Check whether the string terminates with\n0x00\n(UTF-8) or\n0x0000\n(UTF-16). If\nnot, the complete payload shall be discarded and the incident shall be logged. In\ncase of a received REQUEST message (see [PRS_SOMEIP_00055]), addition-\nally, an ERROR message with return code set to\nE_MALFORMED_MESSAGE\n( see\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00191]) shall be sent to the requester.\n6. Perform the re-encoding from UTF-16 to UTF-8 if the on-the-wire encoding is\nconfigured as UTF-16 by\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nstringEncod-\ning\n. The re-encoding from UTF-16BE to UTF-8 shall be done if the configured\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis set to\nmostSignificant-\nByteFirst\n. The re-encoding from UTF-16LE to UTF-8 shall be done if the\nconfigured\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nbyteOrder\nis set to\nmostSig-\nnificantByteLast\n.\n7. Copy the string data (i.e., everything but the BOM and any string termination\nadded during serialization).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136)\n7.4.1.9.6 Vectors and arrays\nSOME/IP supports arrays with static and dynamic length but there is no definition of\nvectors on this abstraction level. Therefore, vectors are mapped to arrays with dynamic\nlength. The SOME/IP specification requires to add a length field of 8, 16 or 32 bit in\nfront of data structures with dynamic length. The length field of arrays describes the\n123 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 126,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_00260] Datatype for the length field of arrays\nd\nIf\nTransforma-\ntionPropsToServiceInterfaceElementMapping\n.\ntransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\ndefines the the data type for the length field of a array,\nthe data shall be:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10076] Serializing arrays\nd\nA array shall be serialized as the concatenation\nof the following elements:\n\u000f\nthe length indicator which holds the length (in bytes) of the following array\n\u000f\nthe array which contains the serialized elements of the array\nwhere the size of the length field shall be determined as specified by\nApSomeip-\nTransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfArrayLengthField\nwhich applies to the array\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10234] Vector representation\nd\nA vector is represented in adaptive plat-\nform by a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith the category\nVECTOR\n. The payload\nis defined by a\ntemplateArgument\nthat points with the\ntemplateType\nreference to\nthe data type of elements that are contained in the vector. Note that vectors are re-\nalized with dynamic sized arrays on SOME/IP level.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10235] Array representation\nd\nAn array is represented in adaptive plat-\nform by an\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith the category\nARRAY\n. The payload\nis defined by a\ntemplateArgument\nthat points with the\ntemplateType\nreference to\nthe data type of elements that are contained in the array. Note that\nCppImplemen-\ntationDataType\nwith the category\nARRAY\nare realized with fixed length arrays on\nSOME/IP level.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nIn case of nested arrays, the same scheme applies.\n[SWS_CM_10222] Setting the size of the length field for arrays\nd\nThe serializing\nSOME/IP network binding shall write the size (in bytes) of the serialized array (without\nthe size of the length field) into the length field.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_-\nCM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nThe layout of arrays with dynamic length is shown in 7.14 and Figure 7.15 where\nL_1\nand\nL_2\ndenote the length in bytes. The serialization of one- and multi-dimensional\ndynamic length arrays is described in the next two subchapters.\n126 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "verbatim_text": "Table 7.2: Example of a serialized associative map\n[SWS_CM_10266] Applicability of mandatory padding after variable length\ndata elements\nd\nAny mandatory padding (see [TPS_MANI_03107] and [TPS_MANI_-\n03073]) after variable length data elements (see [[TPS_MANI_03103], [TPS_MANI_-\n03104], [TPS_MANI_03117] and [TPS_MANI_03105]) shall be applied after the se-\nrialized\nkey\nattribute as well as after the\nvalue\nattribute in case the respective at-\ntributes is typed by a variable length data type. This requirement does not apply for\nthe serialization of extensible structs and methods.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n(see chapter 7.4.1.9.3)\nNote: Adhering to [SWS_CM_10266] is essential to ensure interoperability with the\nAUTOSAR classic platform where maps may be modelled as\nApplicationArray-\nDataType\nwith a\ndynamicArraySizeProfile\nof\nVSA_LINEAR\nwhere each array\nelement is an\nApplicationRecordDataType\nof variable length and thus [TPS_-\nSYST_02126] applies to the individual\nApplicationRecordElement\ns.\n7.4.1.9.8 Variants\nA Variant (type-safe union) can contain different types of elements. For example, if one\ndefines a Variant of type uint8 and type uint16, the Variant shall carry an element of\nuint8 or uint16. When using different types of elements the alignment of subsequent\nparameters may be distorted. To resolve this, padding might be needed.\n[SWS_CM_10088] Default Serialization layout of Variants specified by the union\ndata type in SOME/IP\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P131_291",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10254",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 131,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThis allows the deserializing network binding to quickly calculate the position where the\ndata after the union (Variant) begin in the serialized data stream. This gets necessary\nif the union (Variant) contains data which are larger than expected, for example if a\nstruct was extended with appended new members and only the first \"old\" members are\ndeserialized by the SOME/IP network binding.\n[SWS_CM_10254] Variant length field\nd\nIf attribute\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\nof\nApSomeipTransformationProps\nis set to a value greater 0, a length field shall be\ninserted in front of the serialized Variant for which the\nApSomeipTransformation-\nProps\nis defined.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10255] Variant length field data type\nd\nIf\nApSomeipTransformation-\nProps\n.\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\nis present for a Variant specified the data type of\nthe length field for the Variant shall be determined by the value of\nApSomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\n:\n\u000f\nuint8\nif\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16\nif\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32\nif\nsizeOfUnionLengthField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10226] Serialized Variant size\nd\nThe serializing SOME/IP network binding\nshall write the size (in bytes) of the serialized Variant (including padding bytes but\nwithout the size of the length field and type field) into the length field of the Variant. This\nrequirement does not apply for the serialization of extensible structs and methods.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n(see chapter 7.4.1.9.3)\n[SWS_CM_10227] Length greater than expected Variant length\nd\nIf the length is\ngreater than the expected length of a Variant a deserializing SOME/IP network binding\nshall only interpret the expected data and skip the unexpected.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_-\nCM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\nTo determine the start of the next expected data following the skipped unexpected part,\nthe SOME/IP network binding can use the supplied length information.\nThe type field describes the type of the element. The length of the type field can be 32,\n16, 8 or 0 bits.\n[SWS_CM_10250] Data type for the length field of variants\nd\nThe data type of the\ntype field of a Variant shall be determined using the\nara::core::Variant::index\n()\nmember function. The Variant template class is specified in [17].\nc\n(RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10251] Value of the variant type field\nd\nThe value of the type field shall be\nset to the value which is returned by the\nara::core::Variant::index()\nmember\nfunction and incremented by 1.\nNote: The\nara::core::Variant::index()\nmember function returns a zero-based\nindex of the element hold in the Variant. A negative index represents a valueless\nVariant.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n131 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P132_292",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10098",

      "source_page": 132,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_10098] Possible values of the variant type field\nd\nPossible values of the\ntype field are defined by the elements of the Variant. The types are encoded in ascend-\ning order starting with 1 reusing the index encoding format of the Variant incremented\nby 1. The encoded value 0 is reserved for the NULL type - i.e. a valueless (empty)\nVariant.\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10099] Serialization of variant types\nd\nThe element is serialized depend-\ning on the type in the type field. This also defines the length of the data. All bytes\nbehind the data that are covered by the length, are padding. The deserializer shall skip\nthe padding bytes by calculating the required number according to the formula given in\n[SWS_CM_10088].\nc\n(RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n[SWS_CM_10230]\n{DRAFT}\nData type for size of union field\nd\nIf\nApSomeipTrans-\nformationProps\n.\nsizeOfUnionTypeSelectorField\nis present for a specified\nVariant, the data type of the type selector field for the Variant shall be determined by the\nvalue of\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nsizeOfUnionTypeSelectorField\n:\n\u000f\nuint8 if\nsizeOfUnionTypeSelectorField\nequals 1\n\u000f\nuint16 if\nsizeOfUnionTypeSelectorField\nequals 2\n\u000f\nuint32 if\nsizeOfUnionTypeSelectorField\nequals 4\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211)\n7.4.1.9.8.1 Example: Variant of uint8/uint16 both padded to 32 bit\nIn this example a length of the length field is specified as 32 bits. The Variant shall\nsupport a uint8 and a uint16 as elements. Both are padded to the 32 bit boundary\n(length=4 Bytes).\nA uint8 will be serialized like this:"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthan\nmaximumSegmentLength\n,\nthe SOME/IP event message\nshall be transmit-\nted/received using segmentation as described in [PRS_SOMEIP_00720] and follow-\ning.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_99036] Event message separation time\nd\nIf attribute\nSomeipEventDe-\nployment\n.\nseparationTime\nis set, and segmentation is activated for the corre-\nsponding SOME/IP event message according to [SWS_CM_10454], the segments\nshall be separated in time by this value.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_10455] Method request message segmentation\nd\nIf the attribute\nSomeipMethodDeployment\n.\nmaximumSegmentLengthRequest\nis set to a value,\nand the data length is larger than\nmaximumSegmentLengthRequest\n,\nthe SOME/IP\nrequest message\nshall be transmitted/received using segmentation as described in\n[PRS_SOMEIP_00720] and following.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_99037] Method request message separation time\nd\nIf attribute\nSomeip-\nMethodDeployment\n.\nseparationTimeRequest\nis set, and segmentation is\nactivated for the corresponding SOME/IP method request message according to\n[SWS_CM_10455], the segments shall be separated in time by this value.\nc\n(RS_-\nSOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_99038] Method response message segmentation\nd\nIf the attribute\nSomeipMethodDeployment\n.\nmaximumSegmentLengthResponse\nis set to a value,\nand the data length is larger than\nmaximumSegmentLengthResponse\n,\nthe SOME/-\nIP response message\nshall be transmitted/received using segmentation as de-\nscribed in [PRS_SOMEIP_00720] and following.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_99039] Method response message separation time\nd\nIf attribute\nSomeipMethodDeployment\n.\nseparationTimeResponse\nis set, and segmenta-\ntion is activated for the corresponding SOME/IP method response message according\nto [SWS_CM_99038], the segments shall be separated in time by this value.\nc\n(RS_-\nSOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_10456] Message segmentation for the get and set methods of\nfields\nd\nFor the\nget and set methods\naggregated by a\nSomeipFieldDeploy-\nment\n[SWS_CM_10455] shall apply. For the\nnotifier\naggregated by a\nSomeip-\nFieldDeployment\n[SWS_CM_10454] shall apply.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n[SWS_CM_10457] Small messages segmentation\nd\nFor messages that would fit into\none segment no segmentation (i.e. no\nTP-Header\n) shall be applied.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_-\n00051)\n[SWS_CM_10445]\n{DRAFT}\nSomeIpBurstTransmission\nd\nIf parameter\nSomeipEventDeployment\n.\nburstSize\n,\nSomeipMethodDeployment\n.\nburst-\nSizeRequest\nor\nSomeipMethodDeployment\n.\nburstSizeResponse\nis set to a\nvalue > 1 and the corresponding message is segmented no separationTime shall be\napplied for this number of segments. If not configured,\nSeparationTime\nwill be\napplied between all frames.\nc\n(RS_SOMEIP_00051)\n133 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P134_295",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10458",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 134,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nNote: If\nburstSize\nis set on receiver side it can be used to optimize buffer handling\nfor reception of bursts.\n7.4.1.10 Marker Interface\nOn the AUTOSAR adaptive platform there are use-cases for the utilization of a Servi-\nceInterface that does not have any method, event, or field defined. In other words, the\nexistence of a ServiceInterface by itself represents a valid semantics that has a value\non its own.\nA service instance that corresponds to such a ServiceInterface may be offered with the\nmere intention to signal that the ECU that provides the service instance is becoming\nready for something. So the SOME/IP Service Discovery mechanism is used to indi-\ncate the readiness. But for the communication not SOME/IP but a different protocol will\nbe used.\nFor example an ECU may indicate with a service offer that it is ready to being diag-\nnosed. A tester could then take the existence of the offer as an indication to initiate a\nconnection to the respective ECU.\n[SWS_CM_10458] Handling of an ServiceInterface that does not contain any\nevents, methods, or fields\nd\nIf a\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nis de-\nfined for a ServiceInterface that does not contain any events, methods, or fields and\na\nProvidedSomeipServiceInstance\nis defined in the\nServiceInstanceMani-\nfest\nthat points to the\nSomeipServiceInterfaceDeployment\nin the role servi-\nceInterface then:\n\u000f\nthe ServiceInterface shall be offered over SOME/IP as defined by\n[SWS_CM_00203] which means that the Endpoint Option shall include\nthe IP-Address, Port Number and Protocol as defined by the\nProvided-\nSomeipServiceInstance\n\u000f\nthe Server shall not create a UDP/TCP socket and shall not bind any socket to\nthe configured server address\nc\n(RS_CM_00101)\n7.4.2 Signal-Based Network binding\nThe applications on the adaptive platform communicate with each other in a service-\noriented manner. When exchanging information with software components executed\non an AUTOSAR classic platform which make use of signal-based communication,\na conversion between this signal-based communication and the service-oriented com-\nmunication needs to take place. Hereby the signals of a received signal-based commu-\nnication is being made available as elements of a provided\nServiceInterface\n. The\nsignals of a sent signal-based communication are being made available as elements of\n134 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P135_296",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11269",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 135,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\na required\nServiceInterface\n. The conversion between signal-based communica-\ntion and service-oriented communication may be performed by a software component\non an AUTOSAR classic platform gateway ECU or by an adaptive application on an\nAUTOSAR adaptive platform\nMachine\n.\nThere are two approaches how the signal-based information is made available at the\nadaptive AUTOSAR\nMachine\n:\n\u000f\nNetwork binding (see section 7.4.2.1)\n\u000f\nNetwork binding (see section 7.4.2.2)\n7.4.2.1 Signal-Based SOME/IP Network binding\nThe\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding is currently a specialization of the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding and many aspects of the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding are\nre-used. Instead of replicating many specification items from the\nSOME/IP\nnetwork\nbinding the approach of this\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding chapter is to\nreplicate the chapter structure. Specification items which are applicable to the\nSig-\nnal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding are just referenced, specification items which\nare NOT applicable to the\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnetwork binding are explicitly ex-\ncluded (via reference), and changed specification items are marked and the origin is\nreferenced.\nOne major difference between the SOME/IP network binding and the\nSignal-Based\nSOME/IP\nnetwork binding is the serialization technology. While the SOME/IP network\nbinding only supports SOME/IP serialized payload the\nSignal-Based SOME/IP\nnet-\nwork binding supports the signal-based serialization of Classic platform COM-Stack as\nwell as the SOME/IP serialization of payload (in order to support mixed use-cases).\n[SWS_CM_11269]\n{DRAFT}\nDefinition of serialization technology\nd\nThe serialization\ntechnology is defined by the attribute\nSomeipEventDeployment\n.\nserializer\n. If the\nattribute is set to\nsignalBased\nthen the signal-service-translation is responsible for\nthe handling of the serialization. If the attribute is set to\nsomeip\nthen the SOME/IP\nserializer is responsible for the handling of the serialization.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nSee also chapter 7.4.2.1.8 and chapter 7.4.1.9.\nIn figure 7.16 an example of a mixed serialized service is illustrated. The event\nx\nis\ndefined to use\nsomeip serializer\nwhile event\ny\nis defined to use\nsignalBased\nserializer\n. Both are part of one service and share the service discovery and gen-\neral event handling.\n135 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P136_297",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10174",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 136,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P136_298",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10174",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 136,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.16: Example serialization settings\nThe modeling of the signal-based communication and the mapping between the indi-\nvidual elements of a\nServiceInterface\nto the corresponding\nISignalTrigger-\ning\ns is defined in the chapter Signal-based communication in [5].\n[SWS_CM_10174]\n{DRAFT}\nMix of signal-based and SOME/IP communication\nd\nA\ncombination of signal-based network binding and SOME/IP network binding shall be\npossible in a way to support the reception of a mix of signal-based communication and\nSOME/IP communication within a single UDP datagram or a single TCP stream on one\nUDP/TCP socket. Such a mix can occur when using [18] with enabled PDU-header\noption on the sender side.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204)\nThis allows to define the transport of messages from several services on the same\nsocket, regardless of the serialization setting. Thus messages using the pure SOME/IP\nnetwork binding can be transported together with messages using the signal-based\nnetwork binding on the same socket.\nAlso one service - which consists of events with different serialization technologies (i.e.\nsomeip\nand\nsignalBased\n) - shall be able to be transported on the same socket (this\nis covered by the signal-based network binding).\nBased on [SWS_CM_10000]:\n[SWS_CM_80001]\n{DRAFT}\nSignal-based network binding shall implement\nSOME/IP and SOME/IP-SD\nd\nThe signal-based network binding shall implement the\nSOME/IP Service Discovery Protocol defined in [6] and the SOME/IP Protocol defined\n136 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10172",

      "source_page": 137,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nin [4] (except for the serialization of signal-based payload).\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_-\n00205, RS_CM_00004)\nLength and Type fields shall always be in network byte order ([PRS_SOMEIP_00368]\napplies).\nBased on [SWS_CM_10172]:\n[SWS_CM_80003]\n{DRAFT}\nByte order for signal-based network binding with\nSOME/IP serialization\nd\nIf\nSomeipEventDeployment\n.\nserializer\nis set to\nsomeip\nthen\nthe byte order of the parameters inside the payload shall be defined by\nbyteOrder\nof\nApSomeipTransformationProps\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_SOMEIP_00026, RS_-\nCM_00004)\n[SWS_CM_80004]\n{DRAFT}\nByte order for signal-based network binding with\nsignal-based serialization\nd\nIf\nSomeipEventDeployment\n.\nserializer\nis set to\nsignalBased\nthen\nthe byte order of the parameters inside the payload shall be defined by the respective\npackingByteOrder\nof\nISignalToIPduMapping\nand\nby the\npackingByteOrder\nof\nPduToFrameMapping\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00004)\n[SWS_CM_10240] applies.\n7.4.2.1.1 Service Discovery\nThe section 7.4.1.2 is fully applicable to the signal-based network binding.\n7.4.2.1.2 Accumulation of messages\nBased on [SWS_CM_10387]:\n[SWS_CM_80017]\n{DRAFT}\nData accumulation for UDP data transmission\nd\nTo al-\nlow for the transmission of multiple messages (SOME/IP event, SOME/IP method re-\nquest, SOME/IP method response, signal-based event, and signal-based field notifier)\nwithin a single UDP datagram, data accumulation for UDP data transmission shall be\nsupported.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00004)\n[SWS_CM_10388] applies.\nBased on [SWS_CM_10389]:\n[SWS_CM_80019]\n{DRAFT}\nConfiguration of a data accumulation on a\nPro-\nvidedSomeipServiceInstance\nfor transmission over UDP\nd\nFor a\nProvided-\nSomeipServiceInstance\nall\nmethod\nresponses and\nevent\ns for which the\nudp-\nCollectionTrigger\nis set to\nnever\nshall be aggregated in a buffer until a trigger\narrives that starts the data transmission.\n137 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
