      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P205_369",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11146",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<Field0Name>_Hash:\n5\n<svcId>Field_Get<Field0Name>_In get<Field0Name>;\n6\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<Field0Name>_Hash:\n7\n<svcId>Field_Set<Field0Name>_In set<Field0Name>;\n8\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<Field1Name>_Hash:\n9\n<svcId>Field_Get<Field1Name>_In get<Field1Name>;\n10\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<Field1Name>_Hash:\n11\n<svcId>Field_Set<Field1Name>_In set<Field1Name>;\n12\n// ...\n13\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<FieldNName>_Hash:\n14\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldNName>_In get<FieldNName>;\n15\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<FieldNName>_Hash:\n16\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldNName>_In set<FieldNName>;\n17\n};\nAccording to 7.5.1.1.4 of [22],\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_In\nstructures shall\ncontain as member, the corresponding\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nrepre-\nsenting the value of\nField\nto be set. Conversely,\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>\n_In\nshall contain a single member named\ndummy\nof type\ndds::rpc::UnusedMem-\nber\n(see section 7.5.1.1.1 of [22]) to indicate that the method has no input parameters.\nThe resulting Request Topic data type shall be encoded according to the DDS serial-\nization rules. Unions, such as the\n<svcId>Field_Call\nunion, shall be serialized as\nspecified in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n[SWS_CM_11146] DDS Service Reply Topic data type definition for Field getter\nand setter operations\nd\nAs specified in section 7.5.1.1.7 of [22], the Reply Topic data\ntype is a structure composed of a Reply Header with meta-data and a Return Structure\nwith data. The IDL definition of the Reply Topic data type for the DDS Service handling\nfield getters and setters is the following:\n1\nstruct <svcId>Field_Reply {\n2\ndds::rpc::ReplyHeader header;\n3\n<svcId>Field_Return data;\n4\n};\nWhere:\n<svcId>\nis the corresponding\nserviceInterfaceId\n.\ndds::rpc::ReplyHeader\nis the standard Reply Header defined in section 7.5.1.1.1\nof [22].\n<svcId>Field_Return\nis the union that holds the return values of the correspond-\ning response, according to the rules specified in section 7.5.1.1.7 of [22].\ndds::rpc::ReplyHeader\nshall be constructed as specified in section 7.5.1.1.1 of\n[22].\n<svcId>Field_Return\nshall be constructed as specified in section 7.5.1.1.7 of [22]:\n\u000f\nThe name of the union shall be\n<svcId>Field_Return\n.\n205 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe union discriminator shall be a 32-bit signed integer.\n\u000f\nThe union shall have a default case of type\ndds::rpc::UnknownOperation\n(defined in section 7.5.1.1.1 of [22]) for unsupported and unknown operations.\n\u000f\nThe union shall have a case label for each\nhasGetter\nand\nhasSetter\nattribute\nequal to\ntrue\nin the\nField\ns defined in the\nServiceInterface\nwith the role\nfield\n, where:\n\nThe integer value of the case label shall be a 32-bit hash of the field\ngetter or setter name. That is,\n\"Get<FieldName>\"\nand\n\"Set<Field-\nName>\"\n; where\n<FieldName>\nis the\nshortName\nof the\nField\n. The\nbinding implementation shall compute the hash as specified in section\n7.5.1.1.2 of [22]. Representations of the service interface in OMG IDL [24]\nshall define 32-bit signed integer constants (i.e.,\nconst int32 <svcId>\nField_Get<FieldName>_Hash\nor\nconst int32 <svcId>Field_Set\n<FieldName>_Hash\n) to simplify the representation of the union cases (see\nbelow).\n\nThe member name of the case label shall be\nget<FieldName>\nfor getter\nmethods and\nset<FieldName>\nfor setter methods.\n\nThe type for each case label shall be\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>\n_Result\nfor getter methods and\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Re-\nsult\nfor setter methods, which shall be constructed as specified in section\n7.5.1.1.4 of [22] (see below).\nThe IDL definition of\n<svcId>Field_Return\nis the following:\n1\nunion <svcId>Field_Return switch(int32) {\n2\ndefault:\n3\ndds::rpc::UnknownOperation unknownOp;\n4\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<Field0Name>_Hash:\n5\n<svcId>Field_Get<Field0Name>_Result get<Field0Name>;\n6\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<Field0Name>_Hash:\n7\n<svcId>Field_Set<Field0Name>_Result set<Field0Name>;\n8\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<Field1Name>_Hash:\n9\n<svcId>Field_Get<Field1Name>_Result get<Field1Name>;\n10\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<Field1Name>_Hash:\n11\n<svcId>Field_Set<Field1Name>_Result set<Field1Name>;\n12\n// ...\n13\ncase <svcId>Field_Get<FieldNName>_Hash:\n14\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldNName>_Result get<FieldNName>;\n15\ncase <svcId>Field_Set<FieldNName>_Hash:\n16\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldNName>_Result set<FieldNName>;\n17\n};\nAccording with [SWS_CM_00112] and [SWS_CM_00113], both getters and set-\nters have the same output parameter. Therefore, in accordance with section\n7.5.1.1.5 of [22], both the\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result\nand\n<svcId>\nField_Set<FieldName>_Result\nunions shall be constructed as follows:\n\u000f\nThe union discriminator shall be a 32-bit signed integer.\n206 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 207,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nThe union shall have a case with label\ndds::RETCODE_OK\nto represent a suc-\ncessful return:\n\nThe value of\nRETCODE_OK\nshall be 0, as specified in section 2.3.3 of [19].\n\nThe successful case shall have a single member named\nresult_\nof type\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Out\nto hold the value to be returned\nto the getter, or type\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Out\nto hold the\nvalue to be returned to the setter (see below).\nThe IDL representation of\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result\nis the follow-\ning:\n1\nunion <svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result switch(int32) {\n2\ncase dds::RETCODE_OK:\n3\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Out result_;\n4\n};\nLikewise, the IDL representation of\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Result\nis\nthe following:\n1\nunion <svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Result switch(int32) {\n2\ncase dds::RETCODE_OK:\n3\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Out result_;\n4\n};\nBoth types\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Out\nand its counterpart\n<svcId>\nField_Set<FieldName>_Out\nshall map to a structure with a single member named\nreturn_\nof the\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nrepresenting the value of the\ncorresponding\nField\n.\nThe resulting Reply Topic data type shall be encoded according to the DDS serializa-\ntion rules. Unions, such as the\n<svcId>Field_Return\nunion, shall be serialized as\nspecified in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n[SWS_CM_11147] Creating a DataWriter to handle get/set requests on the client\nside\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataWriter for the Request Topic asso-\nciated with the getters and setters of the\nfield\ns of the\nServiceInterface\n(see\n[SWS_CM_11145]) upon proxy instantiation.\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been advertised with the\nidenti-\nfier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, to ensure\nthe proxy communicates only with the service instance it is bound to, the binding im-\nplementation shall use the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11009] (whose par-\ntition name is\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<reqSvcInId>\"\n) to create the\nDataWriter.\nThe DataWriter shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataWriterQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsField-\nQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\n207 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "source_page": 208,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11148] Creating a DataReader to handle get/set responses on the\nclient side\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataReader for the Reply Topic as-\nsociated with the getters and setters of the\nfield\ns of the\nServiceInterface\n(see\n[SWS_CM_11146]) upon proxy instantiation.\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been advertised with the\nidenti-\nfier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, to ensure\nthe proxy communicates only with the service instance it is bound to, the binding im-\nplementation shall use the DDS Subscriber created in [SWS_CM_11009] (whose par-\ntition name is\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<reqSvcInId>\"\n) to create the\nDataReader.\nThe DataReader shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataReaderQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsField-\nQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00215, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11149] Creating a DataReader to handle get/set requests on the server\nside\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataReader for the Request Topic asso-\nciated with the getters and setters of the\nfield\ns of the\nServiceInterface\n(see\n[SWS_CM_11145]).\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been advertised with the\nidenti-\nfier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, the bind-\ning shall use the DDS Subscriber created in [SWS_CM_11002] (whose partition name\nis\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<svcInId>\"\n) to create the DataReader.\nThe DataReader shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataReaderQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsField-\nQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\n\u000f\nListener\nand\nStatusMask\nshall be set according to the value of\nMethod-\nCallProcessingMode\nthat was selected in the constructor of the\nSer-\nviceSkeleton\nclass:\n\nFor\nMethodCallProcessingMode = kEvent\nor\nkEventSin-\ngleThread\n,\nListener\nshall be set to an instance of the\nDataRead-\nerListener\nclass specified in [SWS_CM_11154], and\nStatusMask\nshall\nbe set to\nDATA_AVAILABLE_STATUS\n.\n\nFor\nMethodCallProcessingMode = kPoll\n,\nListener\nshall remain\nunset, and\nStatusMask\nshall be set to\nSTATUS_MASK_NONE\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n208 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P209_373",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11150",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 209,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11150] Creating a DataWriter to handle get/set responses on the\nserver side\nd\nThe DDS binding shall create a DDS DataWriter for the Reply Topic as-\nsociated with the getters and setters of the\nfield\ns of the\nServiceInterface\n(see\n[SWS_CM_11146]).\nIf the provided or consumed Service Instance has been advertised with the\nidenti-\nfier_type\nattribute set to\nSERVICE_INSTANCE_RESOURCE_PARTITION\n, the bind-\ning implementation shall use the DDS Publisher created in [SWS_CM_11002] (whose\npartition name is\n\"ara.com://services/<svcId>_<svcInId>\"\n) to create the\nDataWriter.\nThe DataWriter shall be configured as follows:\n\u000f\nDataWriterQos\nshall be set as specified in the Manifest, where the\nDdsField-\nQosProps\nelement defines the\nqosProfile\nthat shall be used.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00005)\n[SWS_CM_11151] Calling get/set method associated with a field from the client\nside\nd\nWhen instructed to call the\nGet()\nor\nSet()\nmethod associated with a\nField\nfrom the client side, the DDS binding shall construct a new sample of the corre-\nsponding Request Topican instance of the Request Topic data type defined in\n[SWS_CM_11145]as follows:\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\nRequestHeader\nobject,\n\nrequestId\nshall be set by the underlying DDS implementation according\nto the rules specified in [22].\n\ninstanceName\nshall be set by the binding implementation to the\nservi-\nceInstanceId\nof the remote service instance.\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\n<svcId>Field_Call\nobject, the binding implementation shall\nfirst select the appropriate union case (as specified in [SWS_CM_11145], the\nhash of the field getter/setter's name is the union discriminator that selects the\nunion case). Then,\n\nIf the call corresponds to a getter, the binding shall leave the\ndummy\nmember\nof the\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_In\nstructure unset.\n\nElse, if the call corresponds to a setter, the binding shall set accordingly the\nonly member of the\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_In\nstructure with\nthe new value for the field.\nThat sample shall then be passed as a parameter to the\nwrite()\nmethod of the DDS\nDataWriter created in [SWS_CM_11147] to handle get/set requests on the client side,\nwhich shall serialize the sample according to the DDS serialization rules, and pub-\nlish it over DDS.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213,\nRS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_-\nDds_00015)\n209 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P210_374",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11152",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 210,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n[SWS_CM_11152] Notifying the client of the response to the get/set method\ncall\nd\nTo notify the client application of a response as a result of call to a\nGet()\nor\nSet()\nmethod associated with a\nField\n, the DDS binding implementation shall\ninvoke the\nset_value()\noperation (see [SWS_CORE_00345] and [SWS_CORE_-\n00346]) with the value of the corresponding\nresult_\nmember of either the\n<sv-\ncId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result\nstructure, for get operations; or\n<svcId>\nField_Set<FieldName>_Out\n, for set operations.\nThe associated set operation shall be performed upon the reception of a new Reply\nTopic sample by the corresponding DDS DataReader (see [SWS_CM_11148]). The\nDDS binding shall use the DataReader's\ntake()\nmethod to process the sample. More-\nover, to correlate a request with a response, the binding shall compare the\nheader.-\nrelatedRequestsId\nof the received sample with the original\nrequestId\nthat was\nsent in [SWS_CM_11151]\n13\n. If the\nrelatedRequestId\ndoes not correspond to a\nrequestId\nthat has been sent by the client, the response shall be discarded.\nc\n(RS_-\nCM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00015)\n[SWS_CM_11153] Processing a get/set method call associated with a field on\nthe server side (event driven)\nd\nIn case a\nMethodCallProcessingMode\nof ei-\nther\nkEvent\nor\nkEventSingleThread\nhas been passed to the constructor of the\nServiceSkeleton\n(see [SWS_CM_00130]), the binding implementation shall cre-\nate a\nDataReaderListener\nto process the requests asynchronouslyas described\nin [SWS_CM_11154]and attach an instance of it to the DataReader processing the\nrequests for the getters and setters of the\nServiceInterface\n's\nfield\ns in accor-\ndance with [SWS_CM_11149]. The listener is responsible for identifying the method\nthat shall process the request and dispatch it (see [SWS_CM_11154]).\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220, RS_CM_00221, FO_RS_-\nDds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00016)\n[SWS_CM_11154] Creating a DataReaderListener to process asynchronous\nrequests for field getters and setters on the server side\nd\nAccording to\n[SWS_CM_11149], a\nMethodCallProcessingMode\nof either\nkEvent\nor\nkEventS-\ningleThread\nrequires the instantiation of a\nDataReaderListener\nto process asyn-\nchronously requests on the server side. The resulting listener shall derive from the\nstandard\nDataReaderListener\nclass [19], specifying that the type of the samples to\nbe handled is the Request Topic data type defined in [SWS_CM_11145].\nThe\nDataReaderListener\nshall implement the following method according to the\nspecified instructions:\n\u000f\nAn\non_data_available()\nmethod responsible for reading the received re-\nquests from the DataReader's cacheusing the\ntake()\noperationand dis-\npatching it to the corresponding registered\nSetHandler\norif it applies\nGetH-\nandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00114] and [SWS_CM_00116]). To identify the field of"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthe\nServiceSkeleton\nclass, the operation (i.e.,\nSet()\nor\nGet()\n), and there-\nfore the corresponding handler;\non_data_available()\nshall use the union\ndiscriminator of the\n<svcId>Field_Call\nunion (see [SWS_CM_11145]). In\nthe case of a\nSet()\noperation, the method shall provide the corresponding\nSetHandler\nwith the only member of the received\n<svcId>Field_<Field-\nName>_In\nstructure, which contains the new value to be set. In the case of a\nGet\n()\noperation, the binding shall dispatch to the corresponding\nGetHandler\nif it\nwas registeredor to an internal lookup operation for the current value of the\nfield if it was not.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220, RS_CM_00221,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11155] Processing a get/set method call associated with a field on\nthe server side (polling)\nd\nIn case a\nMethodCallProcessingMode\nof\nkPoll\nhas\nbeen passed to the constructor of the\nServiceSkeleton\n(see [SWS_CM_00130]),\nthe\nProcessNextMethodCall\nmethod is responsible for calling\ntake()\non\nthe DataReader processing the Request Topic associated with the service (see\n[SWS_CM_11145]).\nProcessNextMethodCall\nshall take only the first sample from\nthe DataReader's cache and dispatch it to the corresponding registered\nSetHandler\norif it applies\nGetHandler\n(see [SWS_CM_00114] and [SWS_CM_00116]).\nTo identify the field of the\nServiceSkeleton\nclass, the operation (i.e.,\nSet()\nor\nGet\n()\n), and therefore the corresponding handler, the binding implementation shall use\nthe union discriminator of the\n<svcId>Field_Call\nunion (see [SWS_CM_11145]).\nIn the case of a\nSet()\noperation, the binding shall provide the corresponding\nSetHandler\nwith the only member of the received\n<svcId>Field_<FieldName>\n_In\nstructure, which contains the new value to be set. In the case of a\nGet()\noper-\nation, the binding shall call the corresponding\nGetHandler\nif it was registeredor\ndispatch to an internal lookup operation for the current value of the field if it was not.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220, RS_CM_00221,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008)\n[SWS_CM_11156] Sending a response for a get/set method call associated with\na field from the server side\nd\nThe binding implementation shall send a response upon\nthe return of (1) a\nSetHandler\nin the case of a\nSet()\noperation; (2) a\nGetHandler\nin\nthe case of a\nGet()\noperation where a\nGetHandler\nhas previously been registered;\nor (3) a lookup operation\n14\nas a result of a\nGet()\noperation where no\nGetHandler\nwas previously registered.\nTo send the response, the DDS binding shall construct a new sample of the Reply\nTopican instance of the Reply Topic data type defined in [SWS_CM_11146]as\nfollows:\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\nReplyHeader\nobject,"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P212_377",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11151",

      "source_page": 212,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\nrelatedRequestId\nshall be set to the value of the\nheader.re-\nquestId\nattribute of the request that triggered the method call (see\n[SWS_CM_11151]).\n\u000f\nTo initialize the\n<svcId>Field_Return\nobject, the binding implementation\nshall:\n\nSelect the appropriate union case (as specified in [SWS_CM_11146]), the\nhash of the field's getter/setter method is the union discriminator that selects\nthe union case).\n\nSet the appropriate\n<svcId>Field_Get<FieldName>_Result\nfor\nGet\n()\noperationsor\n<svcId>Field_Set<FieldName>_Result\nfor\nSet\n()\noperations. In both cases, the binding shall select the union case for\ndds::RETCODE_OK\nand set the corresponding structure with the value re-\ntrieved upon the return of (1), (2), or (3).\nThe sample shall then be passed as a parameter to the\nwrite()\nmethod of the DDS\nDataWriter created in [SWS_CM_11150] to handle method responses on the server\nside, which shall serialize the sample according to the DDS serialization rules, an pub-\nlish it over DDS.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00212, RS_CM_00213, RS_CM_00220,\nRS_CM_00221, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00008, FO_RS_Dds_00015)\nThe DDS serialization rules are defined in section 7.4.3.7.\n7.4.3.7 Serialization of Payload\n[SWS_CM_11040] DDS standard serialization rules\nd\nThe serialization of the payload\nshall be done according to the DDS standard serialization rules defined in section\n7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00002)\n7.4.3.7.1 Basic Data Types\n[SWS_CM_11041] DDS serialization of\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory VALUE\nd\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory VALUE\nshall\nbe serialized according to the standard serialization rules for the equivalent DDS\nPRIMITIVE_TYPE\ndefined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21]. [SWS_CM_12020] provides\nthe equivalent DDS\nPRIMITIVE_TYPE\ns for the primitive\nStdCppImplementation-\nDataType\ns with\ncategory\nVALUE defined in [14].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200,\nRS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n[SWS_CM_12020]\nStdCppImplementationDataType\ns with category VALUE\nsupported for serialization\nd"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P213_379",

      "source_page": 213,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00200, RS_CM_00102, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_-\nDds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.2 Enumeration Data Types\n[SWS_CM_11042] DDS serialization of enumeration data types\nd\nEnumeration\ndata types shall be serialized according to the standard serialization rules for DDS\nENUM_TYPE\ndefined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nThe bit bound of the\nENUM_TYPE\nshall be set to the size of the enumeration's underlying\nbasic data type (i.e., the\nPrimitive Cpp Implementation Data Type\naccord-\ning to [SWS_LBAP_00027]) in bits.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.3 Structured Data Types (structs)\n[SWS_CM_11043] DDS serialization of\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory STRUCTURE\nd\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory STRUC-\nTURE\nshall be serialized according to the standard serialization rules for DDS\nSTRUCT_TYPE\ndefined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nOptional members of the structure shall be marked as optional as specified in section\n7.2.2.4.4.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211,\nFO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.4 Strings\n[SWS_CM_11044] DDS serialization of\nStdCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory STRING\nwith string\nshortName\nd\nAn\nStdCppImplementation-\nDataType\nof\ncategory STRING\nshall be serialized according to the standard seri-\nalization rules for DDS\nSTRING_TYPE\ndefined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_-\nRS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n213 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {

      "source_element": "SWS_CM_11046",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 214,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_CM_11046] Encoding Format and Endianness of Strings in DDS\nd\nSection\n7.4.1.1.2 of [21] specifies the standard character encoding format for\nSTRING_TYPE\n:\nUTF-8. The serialized version shall not include a Byte Order Mark (BOM), as byte\norder information is already available in the RTPS Encapsulation Identifier and the\nXCDR serialization format [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202,\nRS_CM_00211, RS_AP_00136, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_-\nDds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.5 Vectors and Arrays\n[SWS_CM_11047] DDS serialization of\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncat-\negory VECTOR\nd\nA\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory VECTOR\nshall be\nserialized according to the standard serialization rules for DDS\nSEQUENCE_TYPE\nde-\nfined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nBinding implementations shall serialize\nVECTOR CppImplementationDataType\ns\nwith more than one dimension, as nested DDS sequences.\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_-\nCM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_-\n00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n[SWS_CM_11048] DDS serialization of\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncate-\ngory ARRAY\nd\nA\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory ARRAY\nshall be se-\nrialized according to the standard serialization rules for DDS\nARRAY_TYPE\ndefined in\nsection 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_-\n00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.6 Associative Maps\n[SWS_CM_11049] DDS serialization of\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncat-\negory ASSOCIATIVE_MAP\nd\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory ASSO-\nCIATIVE_MAP\nshall be serialized according to the standard serialization rules for\nDDS\nMAP_TYPE\ndefined in section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201,\nRS_CM_00202, RS_CM_00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_-\nDds_00007)\n7.4.3.7.7 Variant\n[SWS_CM_11050] DDS serialization of\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncat-\negory VARIANT\nd\nCppImplementationDataType\nof\ncategory VARIANT\nshall be\nserialized according to the standard serialization rules for DDS\nUNION_TYPE\ndefined\nin section 7.4.3.5 of [21].\nc\n(RS_CM_00204, RS_CM_00201, RS_CM_00202, RS_CM_-\n00211, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00007)\n214 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P215_381",

      "source_page": 215,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4.3.8 End-to-end communication protection\nThe present DDS network binding is defined in terms of interactions between\nara::\ncom\nAPIs and standard DDS APIs. Hence, End-to-end communication protection as\ndescribed in sections 7.6.1 and 7.6.2 doesn't apply, because API calls can't be check-\nsummed or payloaded the same way serialized messages are.\nBy no means does this imply that DDS is exempt from E2E protection assurances,\nthey are simply provided by the DDS middleware. Please find below the different kinds\nof faults defined in [7] (derived from ISO-26262-6:2011, annex D.2.4) and their corre-\nsponding DDS/RTPS protection mechanism:\n\u000f\nRepetition, loss, insertion, incorrect sequence, information from a sender re-\nceived by only a subset of receivers, and blocking access to a communica-\ntion channel: submessage 64-bit sequence number, as defined in [20] section\n8.3.5.4 \"SequenceNumber\", and additional SequenceNumber-typed fields in sec-\ntion 8.3.7 \"RTPS Submessages\"\n\u000f\nDelay of information and blocking access to a communication channel:\nLA-\nTENCY_BUDGET\nQuality of Service policy, as defined in [19] section 2.2.3.8 \"LA-\nTENCY_BUDGET\"\n\u000f\nMasquerade or incorrect addressing of information: DDS Security authentication\nplugin, as defined in [26] section 8.3 \"Authentication Plugin\"\n\u000f\nCorruption of information, asymmetric information sent from a sender to mul-\ntiple receivers:\nrtpsMessageChecksum\nunder HeaderExtension submessage\n([RTPS 2.5 or higher]). In absence of this feature, [26] also provides message\nintegrity verification built into its message authentication protocol\n\u000f\nTranslation of these fault conditions into\nara::com::e2e::ProfileCheck-\nStatus\nvalues depends on the specific capacities of the DDS implementation\nto report per-sample the status of the aforementioned protection measures (se-\nquence numbers, latency budget, message authentications, checksums)\n7.5 Security\nIn the following chapter the behavior according to the meta-model of access control\nand secure communication shall be described.\n7.5.1 IAM\nAccess control for Communication Management allows to restrict the instances and\nelements of services that a local application or a\nremote subject\n(e.g., a remote ECU)\nmay request to access. Having access control in place reduces the potential damage\n215 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P216_382",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 216,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthat a compromised application (in case of local IAM) or a compromised ECU (in case\nof remote IAM) can cause.\nFigure 7.17 demonstrates an example scenario where local IAM and remote IAM can\ntake place. Upon a method call from a service, the client's request will be checked by\nthe local IAM to ensure that the application is issuing a legitimate request based on its\nconfigured access rights. After successful authorization, the request will be forwarded\nto the machine where the service is running. When the request arrives at the recipient\nmachine, the remote IAM takes place and a check will be performed to verify if such a\nrequest coming from the given sender ECU was envisioned."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P216_383",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 216,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.17: Local and Remote Identity and Access Management\nThe following assumption has to be held true to realize access control:\n1. Communication between two applications has to be realized by using ara::com\ninterfaces Communication Management to enable access control.\nAll access permissions for Communication Management are modeled using\nComGrant\nmodel elements. A\nComGrant\ncan be used to model access permissions that either\napply to a\nMachine\n-local\nProcess\nor to a remote subject, i.e., either a local Process\nor a remote entity can be the\nsubject\nof the access control policy: If a\nComGrant\nreferences an\nAbstractIamRemoteSubject\nin the role\nremoteSubject\n, then the\nsubjects of the\nComGrant\nare all remote entities that can be identified using the in-\nformation specified in the referenced\nAbstractIamRemoteSubject\n. If a\nComGrant\ndoes not reference any\nremoteSubject\n, then the subjects of the\nComGrant\nare all\nProcess\nes referenced in the role\nprocess\nby\nServiceInstanceToPortProto-\ntypeMapping\ns which reference an\nAdaptivePlatformServiceInstance\nin the\nrole\nserviceInstance\nthat is referenced by the\nComGrant\nin the role\nserviceIn-\nstance\n.\nLocal access control and remote access control may be enforced independently from\neach other.\n216 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P217_384",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10492",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 217,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.5.1.1 Configuration of Access Control\nWhile Identity and Access Management (IAM) serves as an umbrella for access control\non the\nAdaptive Platform\n, the enforcement of access control is implemented in\ndifferent functional clusters such as CM. If no IAM Functional Cluster is instantiated on\na\nMachine\n, then no enforcement of access control by CM is expected.\n[SWS_CM_10492]\n{DRAFT}\nIAM Module Instantiation\nd\nIf no\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine, CM shall perform no access control, i.e., no access\nto any service shall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\nDepending on the architecture and the security model, all local\nProcess\nes might be\ntrusted, thus not requiring local access control. Furthermore, it is possible that all\nremote ECUs are trusted, e.g., because access control is already performed locally.\nFor these cases, there are two configuration options to enable remote access control\nand local access control independently.\n[SWS_CM_10493]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal Access Control Activation\nd\nIf\nIamModuleIn-\nstantiation\n.\nlocalComAccessControlEnabled\nis defined and is set to false, CM\nshall perform no local access control, i.e., no access to any service from a local\nPro-\ncess\nshall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns. If\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine and\nIamModuleInstantiation\n.\nlocalComAc-\ncessControlEnabled\nis not defined or is set to true, CM shall perform local access\ncontrol.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10494]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote Access Control Activation\nd\nIf\nIamModuleIn-\nstantiation\n.\nremoteAccessControlEnabled\nis defined and is set to false, CM\nshall perform no remote access control, i.e., no access to any service from a remote\nsubject shall be restricted because of missing\nComGrant\ns. If\nIamModuleInstanti-\nation\nis defined on the Machine and\nIamModuleInstantiation\n.\nremoteAccess-\nControlEnabled\nis not defined or is set to true, CM shall perform remote access\ncontrol.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10542]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on providing service instances\nd\nIf a\nProcess\nrequests to provide a service instance or any element thereof, but there\nexists no\nComOfferServiceGrant\nthat\n\u000f\ndoes not reference any remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requested\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nin the role\nservi-\nceInstance\nand the\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nis referenced by a\nSer-\nviceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_-\nIAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_90006]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on service discovery\nd\nIf a\nPro-\ncess\nrequests to find a service, but there exists no\nComGrant\nthat\n217 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request and\n\u000f\nthe constructor of the\nServiceProxy\nclass shall throw an exception (see\n[SWS_CM_00131]), or\n\u000f\nthe named constructor function Create() of the\nServiceProxy\nclass (see\n[SWS_CM_10438]) shall return the error code\nComErrc::kGrantEnforce-\nmentError\n.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00006, RS_IAM_00007, RS_IAM_00010)\n[SWS_CM_90001]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on executing methods\nd\nIf a\nPro-\ncess\nexecutes a method of a service interface, but there exists no\nComMethodGrant\nthat\n\u000f\ndoes not reference any remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requested\nRequiredApServiceInstance\nin the role\nservi-\nceInstance\nand the\nRequiredApServiceInstance\nis referenced by a\nSer-\nviceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\n\u000f\nreferences the requested method in the role\nserviceDeployment\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request and\nComErrc::kGrantEn-\nforcementError\nshall be returned in the\nFuture\nof the operator().\nc\n(RS_IAM_-\n00006, RS_IAM_00007, RS_IAM_00010)\nNote:\nIn [SWS_CM_90001], field getters and setters are also methods.\n[SWS_CM_90003]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal a\nSer-\nviceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\n\u000f\nreferences the subscribed event in the role\nserviceDeployment\n,\n218 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request and\nComErrc::kGrantEn-\nforcementError\nshall be returned by the\nSubscribe()\nmethod of the respective\nEvent\nclass.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00006, RS_IAM_00007, RS_IAM_00010)\nNote:\nIn [SWS_CM_90003], field notifiers are also considered as events.\n[SWS_CM_10539]\n{DRAFT}\nLocal access control on receiving triggers\nd\nIf a\nPro-\ncess\nsubscribes to a trigger of a service interface, but there exists no\nComTrigger-\nGrant\nthat\n\u000f\ndoes not reference any remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requested\nRequiredApServiceInstance\nin the role\nservi-\nceInstance\nand the\nRequiredApServiceInstance\nis referenced by a\nSer-\nviceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand the\nServiceInstanceToPortPrototypeMapping\nreferences the re-\nquesting\nProcess\nin the role\nprocess\n,\n\u000f\nreferences the subscribed trigger in the role\nserviceDeployment\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request and\nComErrc::kGrantEn-\nforcementError\nshall be returned by the\nSubscribe()\nmethod of the respective\nTrigger\nclass.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00006, RS_IAM_00007, RS_IAM_00010)\nNote:\nIn case of [SWS_CM_90003] dropping data, the application will not be notified.\nA logging facility for security events is currently not defined in the AUTOSAR Adaptive\nPlatform. Logging violations of access restrictions according to [SWS_CM_90001],\n[SWS_CM_90003], [SWS_CM_10542], [SWS_CM_10543] and [SWS_CM_90006] is\nup to the implementation or specific ECU projects.\n7.5.1.2 Remote Access Control\nIn order to enforce access control on remote entities, the requesting entity first has to\nbe authenticated, i.e., the identity of the\nremote subject\nhas to be established. Then, it\nhas to be decided whether the access is allowed according to the modeled grants.\nThere are currently three ways to authenticate a remote subject:\n\u000f\nTLS:\nIf the remote subject is connected via (D)TLS secure communication, prop-\nerties of this TLS connection and the used certificates can be used for authenti-\ncating the remote subject.\n\u000f\nIPsec:\nIf IPsec is used to establish secure communication, IP related informa-\ntion specified for IPsec configuration can be used for authenticating the remote\nsubject.\n219 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P220_387",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_10495",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 220,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nIP:\nIf IP based communication is used and the authenticity of communication\npartners can be guaranteed by, e.g., the operational environment, IP related in-\nformation can be used for authenticating the remote subject.\nPlease note that while\nSecOC\ncan also provide authenticity of a communication partner,\nit is not used in this section, because the existing association between\nSecOC\nkeys\nand DataIDs already provides a fine grained access control mechanism directly on the\nlevel of secure communication and thus additionally applying IAM would not yield any\nbenefit.\n[SWS_CM_10495]\n{DRAFT}\nTLS-based Authentication\nd\nCommunication Manage-\nment shall associate remote subjects communicating via an established (D)TLS con-\nnection to a\nTlsIamRemoteSubject\naccording to [TPS_MANI_03240].\nc\n(RS_CM_-\n00803)\n[SWS_CM_10496]\n{DRAFT}\nIP and IPsec-based Authentication\nd\nCommunication\nManagement shall associate remote subjects communicating via IP to an\nIPSecI-\namRemoteSubject\nor an\nIpIamRemoteSubject\naccording to [TPS_MANI_03242]\nand [TPS_MANI_03244].\nc\n(RS_CM_00803)\nPlease note that IPsec is usually handled by the OS and may therefore be transparent\nto Communication Management. Therefore, authentication of IPsec secured connec-\ntions relies on tuples of IP addresses, protocols, and ports only.\n[SWS_CM_10497]\n{DRAFT}\nAuthentication Failure\nd\nIf\nIamModuleInstantiation\n.\nremoteAccessControlEnabled\nis set to true and a remote subject cannot be au-\nthenticated, Communication Management shall silently drop all messages from this\nremote subject.\nc\n(RS_CM_00803)\n[SWS_CM_10543]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote access control on providing service in-\nstances\nd\nIf a remote subject provides a service instance or any element thereof, but\nthere exists no\nComOfferServiceGrant\nthat\n\u000f\nreferences the providing remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the provided\nRequiredApServiceInstance\nin the role\nservice-\nInstance\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop all requests to and from this service in-\nstance.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_IAM_00002)\nNote:\nThe remote subject can be identified through the unicast endpoint of the service offer\nmessage.\n[SWS_CM_10498]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote access control on executing methods\nd\nIf a\nremote subject requests the execution of a method of a service interface, but there\nexists no\nComMethodGrant\nthat\n\u000f\nreferences the requesting remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n220 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"

      "source_page": 222,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthen Communication Management shall drop the the subscription request.\nc\n(RS_IAM_-\n00001, RS_IAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10506]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote access control on calling field setters\nd\nIf a\nremote subject requests the execution of a set method of a field, but there exists no\nComFieldGrant\nthat\n\u000f\nhas the parameter\nComFieldGrant\n.\nrole\nset to\nsetter\nor\ngetterSetter\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requesting remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences a\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the event in the role\nserviceDeployment\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_-\nIAM_00002)\n[SWS_CM_10507]\n{DRAFT}\nRemote access control on calling field getters\nd\nIf a\nremote subject requests the execution of a get method of a field, but there exists no\nComFieldGrant\nthat\n\u000f\nhas the parameter\nComFieldGrant\n.\nrole\nset to\ngetter\nor\ngetterSetter\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the requesting remote subject in the role\nremoteSubject\nand\n\u000f\nreferences a\nProvidedApServiceInstance\nin the role\nserviceInstance\nand\n\u000f\nreferences the event in the role\nserviceDeployment\n,\nthen Communication Management shall drop the request.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_-\nIAM_00002)\n7.5.2 Secure Communication\nCommunication in Adaptive Platform can be transported via TCP and UDP. Therefore\ndifferent security mechanisms have to be available to secure the communication. The\nfollowing security protocols are currently supported:\n\u000f\nDDS Security\n\u000f\nSecOC\n\u000f\nTLS 1.2 (see [27])\n\u000f\nDTLS 1.2 (see [28])\n\u000f\nIPSec\n\u000f\nMACsec\n222 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P223_390",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90101",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 223,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe configuration of SecOc and TLS security protocols has a dependency on the net-\nwork binding:\n\u000f\nFor SOME/IP network binding AUTOSAR allows the configuration of secure com-\nmunication for a ServiceInterface by configuring either\nTlsSecureComProps\nmeta-class or\nSecOcSecureComProps\nmeta-class . Both are specialization\nof\nSecureComProps\nclass that is referenced by\nServiceInstanceToMa-\nchineMapping\n. In the case of SecOc additionally\nServiceInterfaceEle-\nmentSecureComConfig\nneeds to be defined and it determines the configura-\ntion settings for the individual ServiceInterface elements. When\nTlsSecure-\nComProps\nis configured, all the service interface elements are secured and\nServiceInterfaceElementSecureComConfig\nis not used.\n\u000f\nFor Signal based network binding, only SecOc configuration is possible, and\nthe configuration is determined by\nSecureCommunicationAuthentication-\nProps\nof a SecuredIPdu referenced by the PduTriggering.\nSecureComProps\nis\nnot used in the context of signal-based network binding.\n\u000f\nFor DDS Network binding, DDS Transport Security over TCP (TLS), DDS Trans-\nport Security over UDP (DTLS) and DDS Security [26] (as transport-independent\nsecurity) are valid, independent and mutually exclusive choices for securing un-\nderlying DDS communications.\nThe configuration of Ipsec (IPSecConfig) in aggregated by a NetworkEndpoint there-\nfore it is independent of the network binding.\nSOME/IP supports one-to-many (unicast) and many-to-many (multicast) communica-\ntion paradigms. These paradigms may switch at runtime for events (see\nmulticast-\nThreshold\n).\nIt is therefore important to be aware of the limitations of the secure channel approach:\n\u000f\nConfidentiality of events\nIf events are transported using UDP and may be sent using multicast, they can-\nnot be guaranteed confidential due to the fact that only SecOC can be used to\nsecure multicast communication and SecOC does not offer confidentiality. This\nrestriction does not apply to DDS Security.\n7.5.2.1 Creation and use of secure channels\n7.5.2.1.1 SOME/IP and DDS network binding\n[SWS_CM_90101]\n{DRAFT}\nSecure UDP and TCP channel creation for TLS, DTLS\nand SecOC\nd\nThe Communication Management software shall create secure UDP\nchannels according to the input for all\nSecureComProps\nreferenced by\nService-\nInstanceToMachineMapping\nin the role\nsecureComPropsForUdp\n. The Commu-\nnication Management software shall create secure TCP channels according to the in-\nput for all\nSecureComProps\nreferenced by\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\n223 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P224_391",
      "source_element": "SWS_CM_90102",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 224,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nin the role\nsecureComPropsForTcp\n. Secure channels may be shared by multiple\nAdaptivePlatformServiceInstance\ns by multiplexing the communication, i.e. by\nreferencing the same\nSecureComProps\nin the same role.\nc\n(RS_CM_00801)\n[SWS_CM_90102]\n{DRAFT}\nUsing secure TLS, DTLS and SecOC channels\nd\nAll\ncommunication triggered by a\nSkeleton\nor\nProxy\nshall be sent via the respective\nsecure channel according to the configuration input. In the configuration the appropri-\nate secure channel is identified by examining the references to\nSecureComProps\nof\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\nfor the\nAdaptivePlatformServiceIn-\nstance\nthat is mapped to an\nEthernetCommunicationConnector\nof a\nMachine\nby this\nServiceInstanceToMachineMapping\n.\nc\n(RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00803)\nThe actual secure channel to be created is determined by the concrete sub-class of\nthe\nSecureComProps\nbase-class.\n[SWS_CM_90201]\n{DRAFT}\nSecure TLS and DTLS channel creation in the\nDDS Network Binding\nd\nSecure channels shall be created as specified in\n[SWS_CM_90101].\nc\n(RS_CM_00801)\n[SWS_CM_90202]\n{DRAFT}\nUsing TLS and DTLS secure channels in the DDS Net-\nwork Binding\nd\nSecure channels shall be used as specified in [SWS_CM_90102].\nc\n(RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00803)\n7.5.2.2 DDS Security\nDDS Security, as defined in [26], is a complementary standard to DDS, providing\ntransport-independent security measures (authentication, secrecy, non-repudiation, in-\ntegrity, access control and logging) without requiring changes to application logic.\nMapping DDS Service Interface and Instance Deployment models, as well as IAM\nCommunications Grant models, to DDS QoS policies, and DDS Security certificate,\ngovernance and permission files is defined by [29].\n[SWS_CM_90218]\n{DRAFT}\nEnforcement of IAM grants through DDS Security\nd\nAdaptive Applications providing or requiring Service Interface Instances through the\nDDS Network Binding shall enforce, when provided, deployed DDS Security policies.\nc\n(RS_IAM_00001, RS_IAM_00002, FO_RS_Dds_00001, FO_RS_Dds_00009)\n7.5.2.3 SecOC\nThe Secure Onboard Communication (SecOC) feature is embedded into the Adap-\ntive Communication Management. The behavioral aspects of the SecOC protocol are\nspecified in the\nPRS_SecOcProtocolSpecification\n.\n224 of 525 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P225_392",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 225,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nOne major goal is to achieve interoperability with the AUTOSAR Classic Platform\nSecOC\nfunctionality. This is especially applicable to the usage of\nUDP multicast\nmes-\nsages (where SecOC is currently the only protocol supported) and secured signal-\nbased communication with AUTOSAR Classic Platform through the signal-based net-\nwork binding.\nThe SecOC secure channel may provide authenticity and integrity."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P225_393",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 225,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.18: SecOC embedded in the Adaptive Communication Management\nIn order to achieve interoperability with the AUTOSAR Classic Platform the SecOC\nshould be applied identically also in Adaptive Communication Management. The au-\nthentication information comprises of an Authenticator (e.g. Message Authentication\nCode) and optionally a Freshness Value.\nThe SOME/IP Message Header as shown in figure 7.19 divided into two parts: Part\nI containing the Message ID and the Length and Part II containing Request ID, Pro-\ntocol Version, Interface Version, Message Type and Return Code(SOME/IP Protocol\nSpecification [4])."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_com_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_C_P226_394",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement",
      "source_page": 226,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Communication Management\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIn figure 7.21 the handling of the SOME/IP payload, the SecOC part, and the SOME/IP\nMessage Header are illustrated. This setup is defined by the AUTOSAR Classic plat-\nform. In order to achieve interoperability the Communication Management shall im-\nplement an identical behavior. It is essential that the Part I of the SOME/IP Message\nheader is NOT covered by the SecOC calculation.\nTo keep the interoperability with the AUTOSAR Classic Platform and provide the op-\ntional Freshness Value Management functionality the Adaptive Communication Man-\nagement will rely on a pluggable Freshness Value Management Library."
    }
  ],
  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Kommunikationsmodell</h4>\n<p><code>ara::com</code> ist die standardisierte Anwendungsoberfläche des Communication-Management-Funktionsclusters. Der Cluster baut und überwacht Kommunikationspfade zwischen Anwendungen auf derselben oder auf verschiedenen Maschinen; die konkrete interne Middleware-Architektur bleibt hingegen Implementierungssache. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1\">SWS CM §7.1.1 „Architectural concepts“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2\">SWS CM §7.1.2 „Design decisions“</a> ordnen die API als protokollabstrahierte, serviceorientierte Schnittstelle ein.</p>\n<p>Aus einem modellierten Service Interface entstehen zwei Rollen: Der Proxy ist die lokale Repräsentation für den Consumer, der Skeleton verbindet die Provider-Implementierung mit der Transportinfrastruktur. Methoden, Events, Fields und Triggers sind die vier vorgesehenen Kommunikationsformen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 „Proxy/Skeleton Architecture“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.2\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.2 „Means of Communication“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3\">SWS CM §7.1.3 „Communication paradigms and Definitions“</a> beschreiben diese Arbeitsteilung.</p>\n<h4>Vom Dienstangebot zur Nutzung</h4>\n<p>Auf Provider-Seite wird ein Skeleton erzeugt und angeboten. Auf Consumer-Seite liefert ein einmaliges <code>FindService</code> die aktuell bekannten Instanzen; <code>StartFindService</code> überwacht Verfügbarkeitsänderungen. Ein Handle identifiziert eine gefundene Instanz und wird zur Proxy-Erzeugung verwendet. Bei temporärer Nichtverfügbarkeit soll der Kommunikationspfad bei einem späteren Angebot erneut aufgebaut werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.1\">SWS CM §7.5.1 „Offer service“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.10\">SWS CM §7.5.10 „Find service“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.11\">SWS CM §7.5.11 „Service proxy creation“</a> liefern die Funktionssemantik.</p>\n<h4>Daten- und Interaktionsformen</h4>\n<p>Events transportieren Daten an angemeldete Consumer; Triggers benutzen denselben Subscription-Mechanismus ohne Nutzdaten. Methoden modellieren Request/Response und können ein <code>Future</code> bereitstellen. Ein Field kombiniert lesenden und schreibenden Methodencharakter mit der Benachrichtigung über Wertänderungen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.3\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.3 „Event and Trigger based communication“</a>, <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.4\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.4 „Method based communication“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.5\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.5 „Field based communication“</a> erklären die Anwendungssicht.</p>\n<h4>Betriebsregeln und Sicherheitskontext</h4>\n<p><code>Subscribe()</code> ist asynchron: Erst <code>kSubscribed</code> im Status oder im Status-Handler belegt eine tatsächlich etablierte Subscription. Empfangene Samples haben einen kontrollierten Besitzübergang und müssen vor Abmeldung oder Proxy-Zerstörung zurückgegeben sein. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12006\">[SWS_CM_12006]</a> und <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00085\">[SWS_CM_00085]</a> sind dafür die maßgeblichen Regeln. E2E-Schutz ergänzt die Datenübertragung um pro Sample auswertbare Statusinformationen; SecOC kann Freshness-Value-Management über die Plattform-Erweiterung einsetzen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4\">SWS CM §7.4 „Safety“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.2\">SWS CM §7.3.2 „Secure Communication“</a> geben den übergreifenden Rahmen vor.</p>\n<h4>Instanzbezug und Bindungsabstraktion</h4>\n<p>Anwendungscode verwendet typischerweise einen logischen <code>InstanceSpecifier</code>; das Manifest löst ihn auf einen oder mehrere bindungsspezifische <code>InstanceIdentifier</code> auf. Damit kann derselbe Anwendungscode mit einer deploymentseitig anderen Bindung arbeiten, ohne deren Repräsentation zu interpretieren. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a> und <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.21\">SWS CM §7.5.21 „Instance Specifier Translation“</a> beschreiben die Übersetzung.</p><div class=\"diagram\" id=\"diag-service-rollen\"><svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" xmlns:xlink=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink\" viewbox=\"0.00 class=\"diagram-note\">Aktivitätsdiagramm: Der logische <code>InstanceSpecifier</code> wird gegen das Manifest auf eine oder mehrere bindungsspezifische IDs abgebildet. Quelle: <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1\">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>\n<p>Die einmalige Dienstsuche <code>FindService()</code> liefert die zu diesem Zeitpunkt passenden Service-Handles; die Ergebnisliste kann leer sein, wenn aktuell keine passende Service-Instanz existiert. Ein technischer Suchfehler wird dagegen als <code>ara::core::Result</code>-Fehler gemeldet, für den die API unter anderem <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> festlegt. Die kontinuierliche Suche mit <code>StartFindService()</code> meldet Verfügbarkeitsänderungen über ihren Handler, der den Container aller passenden Instanzen erhält. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.5.3.2\">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.2 „RadarService Proxy Class Example“</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00122\">[SWS_CM_00122]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00383\">[SWS_CM_00383]</a></p>\n<p>Ein Event-Abonnement hat die Zustände <code>kNotSubscribed</code>, <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> und <code>kSubscribed</code>. Da <code>Subscribe()</code> den Abonnementauftrag zunächst nur entgegennimmt, kann der Status bei der Abfrage noch <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> sein; <code>GetSubscriptionState()</code> und <code>SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler()</code> machen den wirksamen Zustand zugänglich. Wird der Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar, meldet der Handler <code>kSubscriptionPending</code>; nach erfolgreichem Wiederabonnement meldet er <code>kSubscribed</code>. Die Communication-Management-Implementierung muss ein aktives Abonnement nach zeitweiliger Nichtverfügbarkeit wiederherstellen. Hält die Anwendung mehr <code>SamplePtr</code>-Objekte als bei <code>Subscribe()</code> zugesagt, liefert <code>GetNewSamples()</code> den Fehler <code>ComErrc::kMaxSamplesExceeded</code>; dabei können Samples übersprungen worden sein. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310\">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310\">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00315\">[SWS_CM_00315]</a> <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.5.3.5.2\">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 „Monitoring Event Subscription“</a>.</p>\n<p>Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf gibt sofort ein <code>ara::core::Future&lt;Output&gt;</code> zurück. Darüber werden Ergebnis und mögliche Fehler abgefragt: Bei einer konfigurierten Anwendungsfehlerantwort enthält das Ergebnis einen <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> aus der Domäne des <code>ApApplicationError</code>; für einen nicht mehr verfügbaren Dienst ist <code>ComErrc::kServiceNotAvailable</code> festgelegt. Erkennt die Plattform lokal einen Fehler, der den bereits ausgelösten Remote-Aufruf scheitern lässt, muss sie das zugehörige Future mit <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> bereitstellen. Eine eigene Timeout-Überwachung für Methodenaufrufe bietet <code>ara::com</code> nicht; bei verlorener Antwort können blockierende Future-Operationen daher unbegrenzt warten. <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196\">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf stellt Anwendungs- und Verfügbarkeitsfehler über das zurückgegebene Future bereit. Die verlinkten Teilnehmer sind APPLICATION INTERFACE. Quellen: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196\">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440\">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3\">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a>.</p>\n<p>Bei E2E-geschützten Events kann die Anwendung pro <code>SamplePtr</code> mit <code>GetProfileCheckStatus()</code> das Ergebnis der E2E-Prüfung einsehen, beispielsweise <code>kOk</code>, <code>kRepeated</code>, <code>kWrongSequence</code> oder <code>kError</code>. Der <code>SMState</code> verdichtet die Prüfhistorie zur aktuellen E2E-Überwachung; nur bei <code>kValid</code> und einem nicht fehlerhaften Profilstatus darf das zuletzt geprüfte Sample verwendet werden. Schlägt die E2E-Prüfung einer Methodenantwort fehl, setzt die Implementierung einen Fehler aus <code>ara::com::e2e::ComE2EErrorDomain</code> in das zugehörige Promise und damit in das Future-Ergebnis. <div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Kommunikationsmodell</h4>
<p><code>ara::com</code> ist die standardisierte Anwendungsoberfläche des Communication-Management-Funktionsclusters. Der Cluster baut und überwacht Kommunikationspfade zwischen Anwendungen auf derselben oder auf verschiedenen Maschinen; die konkrete interne Middleware-Architektur bleibt hingegen Implementierungssache. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS CM §7.1.1 „Architectural concepts“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS CM §7.1.2 „Design decisions“</a> ordnen die API als protokollabstrahierte, serviceorientierte Schnittstelle ein.</p>
<p>Aus einem modellierten Service Interface entstehen zwei Rollen: Der Proxy ist die lokale Repräsentation für den Consumer, der Skeleton verbindet die Provider-Implementierung mit der Transportinfrastruktur. Methoden, Events, Fields und Triggers sind die vier vorgesehenen Kommunikationsformen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.1 „Proxy/Skeleton Architecture“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.2">EXP ARAComAPI §4.2 „Means of Communication“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS CM §7.1.3 „Communication paradigms and Definitions“</a> beschreiben diese Arbeitsteilung.</p>
<h4>Vom Dienstangebot zur Nutzung</h4>
<p>Auf Provider-Seite wird ein Skeleton erzeugt und angeboten. Auf Consumer-Seite liefert ein einmaliges <code>FindService</code> die aktuell bekannten Instanzen; <code>StartFindService</code> überwacht Verfügbarkeitsänderungen. Ein Handle identifiziert eine gefundene Instanz und wird zur Proxy-Erzeugung verwendet. Bei temporärer Nichtverfügbarkeit soll der Kommunikationspfad bei einem späteren Angebot erneut aufgebaut werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.1">SWS CM §7.5.1 „Offer service“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.10">SWS CM §7.5.10 „Find service“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.11">SWS CM §7.5.11 „Service proxy creation“</a> liefern die Funktionssemantik.</p>
<h4>Daten- und Interaktionsformen</h4>
<p>Events transportieren Daten an angemeldete Consumer; Triggers benutzen denselben Subscription-Mechanismus ohne Nutzdaten. Methoden modellieren Request/Response und können ein <code>Future</code> bereitstellen. Ein Field kombiniert lesenden und schreibenden Methodencharakter mit der Benachrichtigung über Wertänderungen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.3">EXP ARAComAPI §4.3 „Event and Trigger based communication“</a>, <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.4">EXP ARAComAPI §4.4 „Method based communication“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=section.4.5">EXP ARAComAPI §4.5 „Field based communication“</a> erklären die Anwendungssicht.</p>
<h4>Betriebsregeln und Sicherheitskontext</h4>
<p><code>Subscribe()</code> ist asynchron: Erst <code>kSubscribed</code> im Status oder im Status-Handler belegt eine tatsächlich etablierte Subscription. Empfangene Samples haben einen kontrollierten Besitzübergang und müssen vor Abmeldung oder Proxy-Zerstörung zurückgegeben sein. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12006">[SWS_CM_12006]</a> und <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00085">[SWS_CM_00085]</a> sind dafür die maßgeblichen Regeln. E2E-Schutz ergänzt die Datenübertragung um pro Sample auswertbare Statusinformationen; SecOC kann Freshness-Value-Management über die Plattform-Erweiterung einsetzen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS CM §7.4 „Safety“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.3.2">SWS CM §7.3.2 „Secure Communication“</a> geben den übergreifenden Rahmen vor.</p>
<h4>Instanzbezug und Bindungsabstraktion</h4>
<p>Anwendungscode verwendet typischerweise einen logischen <code>InstanceSpecifier</code>; das Manifest löst ihn auf einen oder mehrere bindungsspezifische <code>InstanceIdentifier</code> auf. Damit kann derselbe Anwendungscode mit einer deploymentseitig anderen Bindung arbeiten, ohne deren Repräsentation zu interpretieren. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a> und <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.5.21">SWS CM §7.5.21 „Instance Specifier Translation“</a> beschreiben die Übersetzung.</p><div class="diagram" id="diag-service-rollen"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewbox="0.00 0.00 585.00 96.00" style="max-width:780px">

</div><p class="diagram-note">Aktivitätsdiagramm: Der logische <code>InstanceSpecifier</code> wird gegen das Manifest auf eine oder mehrere bindungsspezifische IDs abgebildet. Quelle: <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.4.8.1">EXP ARAComAPI §4.8.1 „Instance Identifiers and Instance Specifiers“</a>.</p><h4>Verhalten im Fehlerfall</h4>
<p>Die einmalige Dienstsuche <code>FindService()</code> liefert die zu diesem Zeitpunkt passenden Service-Handles; die Ergebnisliste kann leer sein, wenn aktuell keine passende Service-Instanz existiert. Ein technischer Suchfehler wird dagegen als <code>ara::core::Result</code>-Fehler gemeldet, für den die API unter anderem <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> festlegt. Die kontinuierliche Suche mit <code>StartFindService()</code> meldet Verfügbarkeitsänderungen über ihren Handler, der den Container aller passenden Instanzen erhält. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsection.5.3.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.2 „RadarService Proxy Class Example“</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00122">[SWS_CM_00122]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00383">[SWS_CM_00383]</a></p>
<p>Ein Event-Abonnement hat die Zustände <code>kNotSubscribed</code>, <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> und <code>kSubscribed</code>. Da <code>Subscribe()</code> den Abonnementauftrag zunächst nur entgegennimmt, kann der Status bei der Abfrage noch <code>kSubscriptionPending</code> sein; <code>GetSubscriptionState()</code> und <code>SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler()</code> machen den wirksamen Zustand zugänglich. Wird der Dienst vorübergehend nicht verfügbar, meldet der Handler <code>kSubscriptionPending</code>; nach erfolgreichem Wiederabonnement meldet er <code>kSubscribed</code>. Die Communication-Management-Implementierung muss ein aktives Abonnement nach zeitweiliger Nichtverfügbarkeit wiederherstellen. Hält die Anwendung mehr <code>SamplePtr</code>-Objekte als bei <code>Subscribe()</code> zugesagt, liefert <code>GetNewSamples()</code> den Fehler <code>ComErrc::kMaxSamplesExceeded</code>; dabei können Samples übersprungen worden sein. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00333">[SWS_CM_00333]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00315">[SWS_CM_00315]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00701">[SWS_CM_00701]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.5.3.5.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 „Monitoring Event Subscription“</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Zustandsdiagramm: Übergänge des Event-Abonnements bei Dienstverlust und automatischer Wiederherstellung. Quellen: <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00310">[SWS_CM_00310]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00315">[SWS_CM_00315]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_EXP_ARAComAPI.pdf#nameddest=subsubsection.5.3.5.2">EXP ARAComAPI §5.3.5.2 „Monitoring Event Subscription“</a>.</p>
<p>Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf gibt sofort ein <code>ara::core::Future&lt;Output&gt;</code> zurück. Darüber werden Ergebnis und mögliche Fehler abgefragt: Bei einer konfigurierten Anwendungsfehlerantwort enthält das Ergebnis einen <code>ara::core::ErrorCode</code> aus der Domäne des <code>ApApplicationError</code>; für einen nicht mehr verfügbaren Dienst ist <code>ComErrc::kServiceNotAvailable</code> festgelegt. Erkennt die Plattform lokal einen Fehler, der den bereits ausgelösten Remote-Aufruf scheitern lässt, muss sie das zugehörige Future mit <code>ComErrc::kCommunicationFailure</code> bereitstellen. Eine eigene Timeout-Überwachung für Methodenaufrufe bietet <code>ara::com</code> nicht; bei verlorener Antwort können blockierende Future-Operationen daher unbegrenzt warten. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=paragraph.7.4.1.2.6">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.6 „Timeout supervision“</a></p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequenzdiagramm: Ein Request/Response-Methodenaufruf stellt Anwendungs- und Verfügbarkeitsfehler über das zurückgegebene Future bereit. Die verlinkten Teilnehmer sind APPLICATION INTERFACE. Quellen: <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_00196">[SWS_CM_00196]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_10440">[SWS_CM_10440]</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=subparagraph.7.4.1.2.5.3">SWS Communication Management §7.4.1.2.5.3 „E2E error notification“</a>.</p>
<p>Bei E2E-geschützten Events kann die Anwendung pro <code>SamplePtr</code> mit <code>GetProfileCheckStatus()</code> das Ergebnis der E2E-Prüfung einsehen, beispielsweise <code>kOk</code>, <code>kRepeated</code>, <code>kWrongSequence</code> oder <code>kError</code>. Der <code>SMState</code> verdichtet die Prüfhistorie zur aktuellen E2E-Überwachung; nur bei <code>kValid</code> und einem nicht fehlerhaften Profilstatus darf das zuletzt geprüfte Sample verwendet werden. Schlägt die E2E-Prüfung einer Methodenantwort fehl, setzt die Implementierung einen Fehler aus <code>ara::com::e2e::ComE2EErrorDomain</code> in das zugehörige Promise und damit in das Future-Ergebnis. <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90420">[SWS_CM_90420]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90421">[SWS_CM_90421]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_12021">[SWS_CM_12021]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90422">[SWS_CM_90422]</a> <a class="swsref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CM_90477">[SWS_CM_90477]</a></p>
